picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. Pete Fiutak Tue, October 27, 2026 at 11:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas Tech was cruising right along, looking like the star of the Big 12 again after a 53-25 blowout over Arizona State, and then it walked into a wall at Cincinnati, losing with a 37-24 thud. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona football game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 28, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football College football has one of the longest offseasons of any sport, which lends itself to certain players and teams generating a lot of hype and attention. Texas Tech falls squarely in that category, as its seemingly unlimited resources thanks to billionaire booster Cody Campbell made it a go-to place for top transfers out of the portal. But that also led to the ill-fated acquisition of quarterback Brendan Sorsby , who after leaving Cincinnati for Tech was revealed to have bet on college sports. Sorsby was banned by the NCAA, later reinstated, but the backlash led to him leaving the program before ever playing a game. Despite that, Tech was unbeaten before losing last week, dropping to No. 13 in the AP poll and into a tie for second place in the Big 12 with, among other teams, Arizona. That in effect makes Saturday’s matchup an unofficial elimination game for the conference title race. To better understand the Red Raiders, we reached out to Seth Jungman of Staking the Plains for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his eloquent answers to our inarticulate questions: AZ Desert Swarm: Outside of the irony of the first loss coming to Cincinnati, what were the biggest contributors to Texas Tech falling from the ranks of the unbeatens? Seth Jungman: “It’s the thing that I think Texas Tech fans have known, but maybe the national media wasn’t paying attention. I think most fans have known that the offense simply wasn’t very good and the defense isn’t as good as it was last year. Will Hammond is fine, but there’s a reason why the staff went out to get Brendan Sorsby before the season. They knew he probably wasn’t ready, but things happened and here we are. Also, I think it’s incredibly evident that the players who were part of this defense last year were truly special, particularly Jacob Rodriguez, David Bailey, and Romello Height. Getting to the quarterback to wreck offenses was the cheat code last year and this year, that’s simply not happening.” It’s fair to say that Will Hammond was not the first choice to lead this offense. How do you think he has performed to this point? What are his best attributes and where does he lack most? “I thought last week against Arizona State he took a step forward, but against Cincinnati he took two steps back. His best attributes is that he is a natural leader and he wants the ball in his hands and he wants to be the guy. My biggest problem with him is that I think he makes bad game management decisions. Knowing that the team needs points, he’ll heave the ball towards the end zone with a low chance of completion rather than take the play that keeps the drive alive. His lack of understanding of knowing when to take chances and when to churn yards is what bothers me the most.” What is the likelihood that Cameron Dickey will be back for this game? How would that impact the run game and the way J’Koby Williams, who has run for 680 yards and five touchdowns, get used? “I think chances are very good that he returns. It’s been about four weeks from the dreaded high-ankle sprain and that’s about the time. I don’t think it was a bad sprain so this game would seem about right and he was out doing some drills this past week. What Dickey offers is a guy that’s going to bruise and batter the opposing defense while Williams will break a 40-yard run in what looks like a lost play. Quinten Joyner has tried to fill that roll for Dickey, but it’s not the same. Joyner is coming off of ACL surgery and he doesn’t have the same burst he had at USC. I think the staff will likely get back to that Dickey-Williams rotation as soon as possible.” Texas Tech is second in FBS in passes intercepted (13) but has also given up 16 TD passes and is ranked third-worst in the Big 12 in pass defense. How do you expect the defense to try and stop Noah Fifita? “As mentioned above, the Texas Tech defense last year was getting to the quarterback so quickly that teams simply could not function offensively. This year . . . not so much. Fifita has rounded out to be such a good quarterback, I truly expect him to have a very good day. There’s almost no difference between his home and road stats, three picks on the road and just one at home, and he’s throwing for nearly 300 yards every time he steps on the field. That’s the kind of consistency that you expect from a senior and with Fifita’s ability to run to keep the defense honest, I expect him to do what he’s done all year long.” Who are the top defensive players that Arizona has to be most concerned with? “Defensive tackle AJ Holmes is an absolute unit and there aren’t a ton of defensive tackles that truly rush the passer, but he’s one of them. The linebacking corps is incredibly solid with Ben Roberts, John Curry and Austin Romaine. I’ll also add in Brice Pollock at cornerback. The pass defense is struggling a bit, but he’s a solid cornerback that can make plays.” Considering all the money that was spent on this team, and all the national attention it has brought on itself—thanks, Cody Campbell!—does it feel like the season is on the line in this game? How do you expect Tech to respond to that last performance? “As you have already recognized, this team is a quarterback short of maybe what it could have been. I try not to involve myself in the offseason drama. The whole thing was a mess and handled poorly. I think we’ve all moved on, but I know it still lingers and I think that Sorsby would have made a significant difference in the offense. For what Joey McGuire preaches, yes, the season is on the brink because the goal is to win the Big 12 and make the playoffs. I don’t know that a Big 12 team with two losses makes the playoff and I also don’t think that a 2-loss Big 12 team makes the championship. “I do expect Texas Tech to play much better than what they did against Cincinnati and I think it will be a much more competitive game. I also realize that Arizona’s defense is no joke and the Texas Tech offense has really only played well against defenses that aren’t very good. The offense and defense for the Red Raiders have a lot to prove against Arizona.” Prediction time. Does Arizona end the Red Raiders’ 12-game home win streak and continue its push toward the Big 12 title game or does Texas Tech get back on track? Give us a score pick. “My gut tells me that this will be an incredibly close game and Vegas thinks so as well. With a touchdown advantage, the line now sits at Texas Tech -3.5. I tend to agree, that despite the flaws that were on display against Cincinnati, I think Texas Tech does win the game, but I’d take Arizona and those points. Something like 37-34 is what I see the final score being.” Next 3 weeks could decide Big 12 football title game participants Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 9 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Arizona Wildcats and Texas Tech Red Raiders meet on Saturday in Lubbock in a Top 25 showdown that could have major implications on the Big 12 Championship race. Both teams enter Week 9 at 6-1 overall and 3-1 in Big 12 play, but they're coming off completely different Saturdays. Arizona made another statement by crushing Iowa State 39-3, while Texas Tech suffered its first loss of the season in a 37-24 road defeat at Cincinnati. Now, Texas Tech returns home to a place where it has won 12 straight games, while Arizona gets another opportunity to prove it belongs among the top contenders in the Big 12. The matchup also features an intriguing battle between Noah Fifita and an aggressive Texas Tech defense that leads the country with five pick-sixes this season. Here is everything you need to know about Arizona vs. Texas Tech in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Saturday's Big 12 showdown. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Texas Tech -3.5 Over/Under: 54.5 Moneyline: Arizona +134/Texas Tech -160 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Arizona's Passing Game vs. Texas Tech's Defense? The Red Raiders' defense has been underwhelming, at best. Texas Tech ranks 14th in the Big 12 Conference in passing yards allowed per game, ranking only ahead of Cincinnati and West Virginia. Now, this secondary does have 13 takeaways, which is tops in the Big 12. But that also tells me that they may be too aggressive , at times. And now they have to slow down Noah Fifita, who doesn't make many mistakes. He's thrown 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions this season and has the deepest wide receiver corps in the entire Big 12. Whoever wins this match up will win the game. Houston vs. Utah Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 31, Texas Tech 24 Texas Tech was exposed last week at Cincinnati. Yes, they have talent, but they haven't been able to put it all together this season. And after Saturday, there's no evidence that it's magically going to happen against one of the most underrated teams in the country, Arizona, who is playing some of the best football in America right now. Since losing to BYU on the road (a game they led in the second half), Arizona has won five-straight games by an average of nearly 24 points. I haven't even talked about the other side of the ball, where Arizona is Top 5 in passing defense in yards allowed per game, and ranked 3rd in the Big 12 in yards allowed per carry (3.1). The front seven has been outstanding, as that impressive run defense has done it against the Top 2 rushing offenses in the league (West Virginia, Cincinnati). They've racked up 24 sacks in seven games, good for second in the Big 12, and now take on a Texas Tech offensive line that has been spotty, at best, throughout the season. Also, in a game that could come down to the final drive or two, Arizona's red zone defense ranks tops in the Big 12, while Texas Tech comes in at No. 14. And as the game wears on, the Tech defense could get worn down. Tech is second-to-last in the Big 12 in Time of Possession, while Arizona is in the Top 5, this despite having a pass-heavy offense. The icing on the cake on my pick? Special teams. Arizona is the best punt returning team in the Big 12. Texas Tech ranks 13th. These little things in a tough Top 25 match up can be the difference. And they will be come Saturday in Lubbock. And if you want to know where the sharp money is: 62% of the tickets are on Texas Tech, but over 80% of the money is on Arizona. The line opened up at Arizona +4.5 and is down to +3.5. If you can still get more than a field goal, jump on it. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. In all, Cincy averages 39 rushing attempts per game while throwing the ball only 33.8 times per game. picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Auburn Preview: Rebels Look to Bounce Back Against Tigers - SEC Country Skip to content Alabama Mississippi State South Carolina Instagram X-twitter Youtube Search Search Shop Alabama Stephan Stroud October 28, 2026 The Ole Miss Rebels return to Oxford this weekend for a crucial SEC matchup against the Auburn Tigers, with both teams looking to respond after disappointing losses. No. 12 Ole Miss will try to protect its home field and strengthen its postseason hopes, while Auburn hopes to rebound from a difficult defeat against LSU. Ole Miss enters Saturday’s contest at 5-2 overall and 3-2 in SEC play after falling 34-27 to Texas. Auburn sits at 4-3 overall and 2-3 in conference play following a 38-17 loss to LSU. With the regular season entering its final stretch, both programs need a strong performance to build momentum. Pete Golding and Ole Miss Look to Respond First-year Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding faces an important test as the Rebels attempt to recover from their loss in Austin. Ole Miss showed plenty of fight against Texas, erasing a 21 point deficit to tie the game before ultimately coming up short. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss will once again lead the Rebels’ offense. Chambliss has thrown for 1,926 yards and 16 touchdowns this season, establishing himself as one of the SEC’s most productive passers. His mobility and ability to extend plays make him especially dangerous when the pocket breaks down. Latest episode SEC Country Podcast New shows Monday & Wednesday Airing It Out with Aaron Murray · Oct 28 The Rebels will also have to adjust without running back Kewan Lacy, who is expected to miss Saturday’s game with a shoulder injury. Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight could receive expanded opportunities in the backfield. Golding will also challenge his defense to contain Auburn’s mobile quarterback and prevent the Tigers from establishing their rushing attack. Alex Golesh and Auburn Seek an Upset Auburn head coach Alex Golesh enters his first season with the Tigers looking to get his team back on track. Auburn delivered one of the season’s biggest surprises by defeating Georgia on the road, but the Tigers struggled against LSU the following week. Quarterback Byrum Brown is the centerpiece of Auburn’s offense. The dual-threat signal caller has thrown for 1,365 yards and eight touchdowns while rushing for 480 yards and six scores. Brown’s running ability creates additional problems for opposing defenses, forcing defenders to account for him on designed runs and when passing plays break down. If Auburn can establish its ground game, it could put pressure on an Ole Miss defense that has struggled against mobile quarterbacks. Golesh will also need improved protection from his offensive line after LSU recorded seven sacks against Auburn. Giving Brown enough time to operate could be essential to keeping the Tigers competitive. Key Matchups to Watch The biggest matchup will be Brown against the Ole Miss defense. If the Rebels limit his rushing production, Auburn could struggle to sustain drives. On the other side, Chambliss must capitalize on Auburn’s defensive weaknesses while avoiding costly turnovers. Without Lacy, the Rebels will also need contributions from their other running backs. Final Thoughts Ole Miss has the advantage of playing at home, but Auburn has already demonstrated that it can compete with the SEC’s top programs. Both teams need a complete performance, and whichever side controls the line of scrimmage and protects the football could have the upper hand. Kickoff is scheduled for Saturday, October 31, at 12:45 p.m. ET on the SEC Network. picks.headline: Behind Enemy Lines: Auburn-Ole Miss preview with Sam Hutchens
picks.blurb: This week, we reached out to Sam Hutchens, the Ole Miss beat reporter for The Clarion-Ledger , for the inside scoop on Auburn's Week 9 opponent, the Ole Miss Rebels. This week's conversation with Hutchens focuses on the Rebels recent loss to Texas, the loss of a key player, former Tigers who are shining in Oxford, and much more. Here is this week's Behind Enemy Lines featuring Sam Hutchens of The Clarion-Ledger. What was your biggest takeaway from Ole Miss' recent loss to Texas? SH: "Ole Miss isn't good enough to dig itself out of huge holes. The Rebels were close to doing it in Austin, but Pete Golding was correct when he said they need to be more consistent." Kewan Lacy will not play on Saturday. What does the Ole Miss run game look like without him? SH: "There's a chance it's still pretty good. Makhi Frazier and JT Lindsey have been serviceable backups all year. Look for young Shekai Mills-Knight, who absolutely could be a future RB1 in the SEC, to get more carries too" A handful of former Tigers are with Ole Miss now, including Horatio Fields and Jay Crawford. How much impact have they made since joining the team? Do you expect either of them to dictate the outcome of Saturday's game? SH: "Both players have been solid transfer portal adds. Fields has been a little bit of an unexpected bright spot. He has the second-most catches on the team among receivers, behind Deuce Alexander. Going into the year, he wasn't the player many projected as the WR2." Which Tigers have your attention ahead of the game? SH: "Byrum Brown is the player I'm most excited to see. The Ole Miss rushing defense has been vulnerable at times this season, and the Rebels haven't generated pressure consistently. Maybe a recipe for Brown to shine." Ole Miss wins on Saturday if.... SH: "It turns the ball over one time or less. The Rebels are fantastic in home games over the past few seasons. They don't need a perfect game to win, but they must avoid self-inflicted errors." away.headline: LSU football injury report puts Auburn's tackles under the gun
away.blurb: LSU will see EDGE Princewill Umanmielen's return to the field this coming Saturday after his name was not on the injury report for the Auburn game. Jacob Strand, who was formerly playing in the interior earlier this season, has gotten significant snaps at left tackle of late. He and Jo Simmons have a massive test this coming week against Umanmielen, who was previously questionable after missing most of the game against Mississippi State with an upper-body injury. We'll see if the Auburn offensive line is ready to protect quarterback Byrum Brown against it. Stanton Ramil graded out as an 80 on the right edge against Georgia in the epic Deep South's Oldest Rivalry upset . The interior held up remarkably well, with Wilson Zierer and Kenneth McManus taking starter snaps. Brown and Jeremiah Cobb showed out against the Dawgs with their best outings of the season. The Ole Miss transfer Umanmielen immediately puts one of Golesh's recent big decisions to the test. Not only is Umanmielen a handful, but Tennessee transfer Jordan Ross is also elite. Ross had six tackles and a sack against State this past Saturday. Ross has three sacks this year, which ranks third behind defensive tackle Deuce Geralds's five and Umanmielen's eight. The group is even playing without Gabriel Reliford, who tore his ACL in the spring. The roster Lane Kiffin recruited has an embarrassment of riches in Baton Rouge. If you're looking for ways to nab an upset on Saturday and prove the Plains is haunted for favored opponents , controlling the clock is one of the most obvious. Brown is the ultimate wild card for Auburn. If he can keep LSU's defense guessing, opening up running lanes in the middle for Auburn when LSU's linebackers drop into coverage, perhaps Cobb, Omar Mabson, and the rest of the running backs could be difference-makers in a pivotal SEC clash.

(AP) — Mississippi running back Kewan Lacy will miss this week's game against Auburn after dislocating his shoulder during the third quarter of Ole Miss' loss to Texas , Rebels coach Pete Golding said Monday. "It wasn't exactly what it was before, it was different," Golding said. "Obviously, he's not going to play this week." Recurring injuries to the left shoulder have troubled the preseason All-America selection , who rushed for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns during the 2025 season. A separate shoulder injury during a victory over LSU followed a lower leg injury in the season-opening win over Louisville . Lacy was sidelined against Florida before an open date and a seven-carry performance at Vanderbilt . Lacy had a season-high 122 yards in a victory over Missouri before the injury against the Longhorns. "We're going to evaluate that moving forward, kind of what it looks like," Golding said of Lacy's prospects for returning to the field later this season. "But there's no chance that we're going to try that at all this week." Lacy has rushed for 352 yards and five touchdowns this season. In his absence, Ole Miss is expected to deploy a four-player rotation headed by Michigan State transfer junior Makhi Frazier. Senior Joshua Dye and sophomores JT Lindsey and Shekai Mills-Knight have played in reserve roles, but Frazier has gotten extensive playing time, rushing for 301 yards. "We're going to need all those guys moving forward," Golding said. "We need to do a good job in that room creating roles for them, allow them to execute throughout the week so we can play better on Saturday." LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer return with their picks for the weekend's top games Getty Images Another weekend in college football , another carnage-filled Saturday. This feels like 2007 all over again, thanks to the pure chaos that has ensued over the last two weeks within the top 25. At this point, we're not expecting anything less on Halloween in Week 9, despite only two matchups pitting nationally ranked teams -- the SEC's Georgia vs. Florida showdown from Atlanta and Arizona vs. Texas Tech in the topsy-turvy Big 12. Only three unbeatens in the Power Four remain as the season approaches its final month, with the first CFP rankings set to debut in less than a week. We hope you're betting responsibly this fall, considering this parity-rich party nationwide that shows no signs of ceasing. Season results : Brad Crawford (47-24 straight up, 35-35-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (51-20 straight up, 38–32-1 ATS) My colleague's hot streak continues. After tying things up at midseason against the spread, Hummer's sizzling Week 8 effort has pushed him out front. It's quite humbling for yours truly, whose multi-year reign atop the picks mountain is in serious jeopardy. Perhaps Saturday afternoon comes up aces for me, and we enter November tied again after a rally. On the flip side, Hummer's could swell. No. 25 Wisconsin at Iowa (-3.5) Hummer ( Wisconsin +3.5) : These two teams do the same things well: Run the ball, stop the run. The Hawkeyes are a better rushing offense, while Wisconsin, with Colton Joseph , has the more dynamic option at quarterback -- he uses his legs a lot. To me, this game comes down to which team can avoid turnovers. They've been a killer in losses for Iowa this season. Iowa avoids those against the Badgers and wins a classic Big Ten slugfest at home. The Badgers cover, though. … Iowa 20, Wisconsin 17. Crawford (Wisconsin +3.5) : Had a feeling the Badgers would be ranked at some point this season after watching the opener against Notre Dame . The operation just looked more fluid, despite the final score in a matchup that was more competitive than the final outcome. I believe oddsmakers are giving too much respect to the Hawkeyes here playing at home. An outright win could move the Badgers inside the top 20 of the CFP selection committee's first rankings next week. I'll go ahead and take this one as my upset special in Week 9. ... Wisconsin 23, Iowa 20. No. 22 Arizona at No. 13 Texas Tech (-5.5) Hummer (Texas Tech -5.5 ): A critical matchup in the Big 12 race, the Red Raiders are facing their toughest test since Houston in Week 2. The Wildcats have put up points in bunches this season. But I will say the one week the Wildcats struggled was against BYU , when their run game was bottled up by BYU's defensive front. That's a major potential advantage for Texas Tech in this matchup. The Red Raiders are an excellent front seven and should win that matchup. Can Texas Tech score enough to win this one? It's been a struggle at times, but they get it done. … Texas Tech 27, Arizona 20. Crawford (Texas Tech -5.5) : This is the week we'll be talking about the Wildcats nationally if Arizona finds a way to beat Texas Tech in Lubbock. I don't think it happens, however. The Red Raiders' backs are against the wall in this spot, knowing another loss tanks any shot at reaching the CFP -- or even getting back to the Big 12 title game as the defending league champions. Will Hammond does not have a multi-touchdown outing this season as a passer, but this could be the weekend it finally happens at home. I trust Texas Tech more in this spot than Arizona. ... Texas Tech 31, Arizona 24. Auburn at No. 12 Ole Miss (-12.5) Hummer ( Auburn +12.5): Auburn has struggled this year against above-average defensive fronts. The Rebels aren't elite in that area, but they do blitz a ton and create a lot of havoc around the line of scrimmage. It's going to be up to Byrum Brown to pick up those blitzes and extend plays with his feet. Even without Kewan Lacy , Trinidad Chambliss allows them to score enough. The question is whether Auburn can keep up. I think the Tigers do enough to cover. … Ole Miss 34, Auburn 24. Crawford (Auburn +12.5) : Life in the SEC is hard. Auburn goes from beating Georgia in Athens one week to getting housed on The Plains by another nationally ranked foe the next. Rinse, repeat. If the Tigers had trouble defending Sam Leavitt and that LSU offense, they're going to have equally as much trouble this weekend in Oxford against Trinidad Chambliss. We've seemed to have dismissed his Heisman hopes after the loss at Texas , and that's unwise. Ole Miss gets Georgia coming up, and there are several more opportunities to shine, including this one. I do still have questions about this Ole Miss defense, however. ... Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27. Minnesota at No. 4 Indiana (-20.5) Hummer ( Minnesota +20.5) : That feels like an aggressive line based on what we've seen from Indiana 's offense of late, right? The Gophers are a top-30 defense in terms of yards allowed per play and should be able to challenge Indiana the way Nebraska , Ohio State and Michigan have in recent weeks. The question becomes, can Minnesota score enough to make this a game? The Gophers are 118th nationally in yards per play and have only scored more than 21 points against Power Four competition once this season. It's going to be tough for Minnesota to manufacture points, but the Gophers do enough. … Indiana 27, Minnesota 10. Crawford (Minnesota +20.5) : Can Indiana cover a three-touchdown spread? I have my doubts with Josh Hoover back there. Maybe this is the week the Hoosiers figure it out in the passing game, but the Gophers are sound on the back end and aren't likely to give up explosive plays. I've moved off Indiana in the elite tier of playoff contenders, but the Hoosiers should win here and be ranked inside the top 5 in next week's first CFP rankings. ... Indiana 31, Minnesota 17 . No. 17 Florida vs. No. 3 Georgia (-10.5) Hummer (Florida +10.5) : Was Florida's defensive performance against Texas an aberration or the new norm? That's the big question entering this game. The Gators are 121st nationally in passing yards per game, and the Bulldogs are a top-30 passing offense. That should be a big advantage for UGA. But that unit largely held Texas in check. Otherwise, this is a reasonably even matchup across the board. Georgia's O-line is better -- yes. Florida matches up well otherwise. Georgia wins this game coming off the bye week. The Georgia Bulldogs currently have a 71 percent chance to make the College Football Playoff, according to the A to Z Sports CFP predictor . If Georgia beats the Florida Gators on Saturday in Atlanta, the Bulldogs' chances of making the playoff jump to 83 percent. This won't be an easy task for Georgia. The Gators have been up and down this season. They looked dominant in a 52-28 win over Ole Miss before losing back-to-back games to Missouri and South Carolina. Then they bounced back with a win over Texas two weeks ago (the Gators were off last weekend). Florida isn't consistent, but they're dangerous. ESPN's Greg McElroy, though, has Georgia beating Florida by two scores. "Does Georgia's caution keep Florida around?" said McElroy while previewing this weekend's biggest games. "Look, Georgia goes for it less than any team in the FBS on fourth down, and they run fewer plays per game than most teams in the country. That's a formula for winning comfortably without covering a massive number because punts and field goals leave the door ajar, and if Georgia gets ahead early, then Smart will happily sit on it and try to pound away. "So here's what I'm thinking: these are the two biggest matchups in the game and they both belong to Georgia's offense. The short passing game against a defense that has struggled to stop it, and third down against a defense that has struggled to get off the field. Florida's road win at Texas was very real, but Georgia's front takes away the run game, and that's what made that upset possible. I'm taking Georgia to win the game 34-20. I think Florida did look really impressive on that road trip to Austin. They came home with a massive souvenir, but this is a different animal. Georgia now will be healthy coming out of the bye, and I think they've been excited about this opportunity to host this game in Atlanta." Georgia and Florida usually play in Jacksonville, but they're set to play in Atlanta this season (and in Tampa next season) due to renovations at EverBank Stadium. Former athletic director Mack Rhoades took a separation agreement in November 2025, leaving Aranda's future in doubt under new athletic director Doug McNamee. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman, recently brought in from Kansas State , will serve as the interim coach as Baylor looks to reach bowl season. The Baylor defense was never the issue this season, allowing an average of 16.1 points per game. The offense, under transfer quarterback DJ Lagway, has severely struggled with coordinator Jake Spavital. The Bears sit outside the top 110 in Success Rate on offense, relying on pass explosives as the only means of creating scoring opportunities. Despite the struggles as a whole, Lagway has seen improvement from his days at Florida with an increase in big-time throws and a lower turnover-worthy play rate. The Bears struggle in scoring position, averaging just 3.3 points on 50 offensive possessions inside the opponent's 40-yard line. Red-zone efficiency has been a constant failure all season, ranking 121st in touchdown percentage. Only half of the 30 possessions that made it into the red zone have resulted in a Baylor touchdown. UCF had one of the more advantageous spots of the entire college football calendar when hosting BYU , as the Cougars were coming off a program-defining win over Notre Dame . The overtime game provided all the thrills for a college football masterpiece, as the Knights took a field-storming victory with an 89% post-game win expectancy. Backup quarterback Keyone Jenkins led UCF to four methodical drives and an explosive passing attack, tossing six explosives through the air. The defense had the assignment of slowing down Heisman hopeful Bear Bachmeier , and it limited the BYU quarterback to just 37 rushing yards on 15 carries. The biggest factor was basic fundamentals, as the Knights missed just nine tackles in the game to add on a PFF tackling grade that ranks in the top 25. The Cougars' high-octane offense was limited to just a single rush explosive. It makes sense considering UCF's defense ranks 15th in Line Yards and top-40 in Rush EPA allowed. The handicap on this game forces handicappers to look beyond the advanced statistics, as the Baylor program is in flux. Klanderman isn't expected to win the job as Baylor's head coach, as McNamee has made it clear a coach with Texas roots and an offensive mindset will be the next hire. The downstream effect of the coaching search could create outside noise for coordinators and players looking for their next stop if they don't make a bowl game. Statistically, Baylor could have a hard time generating points against the UCF defense. The Bears have generated plenty of available yards to create scoring opportunities, but a rank outside the top 100 in Finishing Drives will go against a Knights defense that's 32nd in limiting opponents in scoring position. With the expectation that UCF will have a hangover from one of the most electric college football games of the season, a first-half under is the look from a statistical and spot perspective. There are also advantages for UCF in the run game against the Baylor defense. The Bears have a top-10 unit in terms of Rushing Success Rate allowed but have a mid-FBS average of 50% against teams that use inside zone. The Knights run a heavy amount of inside zone through Jenkins and running back Duke Watson . A boost could be in store if quarterback Alonza Barnett III returns from a hamstring injury. The James Madison transfer suited up for the BYU game but did not play for the fifth straight game. Any contribution from Barnett would further solidify UCF's position. Pick: 1H Under 24.5 · UCF ML (-110 or Better) Florida entered the bye week on a high note, beating a top-10 team on the road for the first time since 2012. The Gators remain at two losses on the season in the thick of the SEC race and a potential spot in the College Football Playoff, but a date with Georgia in the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party comes first. The biggest takeaway from the victory over Texas came from backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. tossing a couple of touchdowns in a mistake-free game. The sophomore completed 22-of-35 passes while chipping in 50 rushing yards with an even split of scrambles and designed run calls. On the other side, the defense continues to rank as one of the best in the nation when creating chaos. The top-10 Havoc numbers are led by 53 tackles for loss , nine forced fumbles and 34 passes defensed. Five players on the defensive line have generated double-digit pressures, while seven different defenders have multiple pass breakups. The issue with Florida's defense is its performance close to the goal line, ranking 95th in red-zone defense. The Gators have allowed 40 opponent possessions to cross the 40-yard line and are giving up an average of 4.4 points per trip . Georgia's first loss to Auburn in nine years comes as a result of ball protection. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was responsible for two interceptions and a fumble, an uncharacteristic set of events for the senior. Up until the Alabama game in Week 6, Stockton managed to throw just six interceptions and lose three fumbles since the beginning of the 2025 season. In the past two games, the Georgia quarterback has committed two fumbles and three interceptions . There's the case that Stockton had too much of the load against Auburn, taking a critical hit in the first series of the game. Running back Chauncey Bowens has missed multiple games with injury, while Nate Frazier was ineffective coming off a rib injury, finishing with less than 20 rushing yards. The bye week should provide the best health for the offense in weeks, as head coach Kirby Smart described Bowens as day-to-day . Stockton should also be fully recovered from any shoulder or concussion symptoms. The Bulldogs defense continues to be one of the best nationally in defending the run, ranking top-25 in Rushing Success Rate allowed and Defensive Line Yards. Georgia grades out as one of the best tackling teams nationally, as no individual player has missed more than five tackles this season . Cornerback Ellis Robinson IV has been one of the best at shutting down wideouts all season with five pass breakups and an interception. Defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann has been excellent in disguising blitzes this season, as the highest tally of pressures this season comes from linebackers Chris Cole and Raylen Wilson. The Gators have struggled to run the ball of late, posting a Stuff Rate above the national average in the last three SEC contests against Texas, South Carolina and Missouri . Florida has three primary run concepts in the arsenal: outside zone, counter and power. The most successful and explosive of the group comes from power attempts with a heavy box, led by running back Jadan Baugh. The junior has 100 more rushing attempts than any other player on the team, running an even split of zone read and non-zone read concepts. Despite the highly successful numbers against zone read and counter, Georgia has been horrific against power concepts this season . The Bulldogs have elite numbers in Defensive Finishing Drives and red-zone prevention, ranking fifth in red-zone drives allowed. Although only 15 drives have passed the Georgia 20, the Bulldogs have allowed 14 scores, with 11 of the 15 drives resulting in a touchdown . On the other side of the ball, Georgia has been a pure zone-read team with a heavy batch of inside zone with 11 and 12 personnel. Nearly every run concept from the Bulldogs comes in well above the national average in Success Rate and EPA, but inside and outside zone read produce an explosive on one of every five attempts. Florida has been successful against outside zone but has yet to see an offense execute with two-tight end sets. Georgia should thrive in passing downs, as the Gators sit outside the top 90 in Success Rate and EPA allowed when opponents are off schedule . Action Network's Betting Power Ratings call for Georgia to be favored by 10, giving Florida a slight edge in the spread department. Any number at 13 or better will generate Gators tickets, while any dip below 11 is sure to see steam on the Bulldogs. The better wager comes on the over for a number of reasons. Florida has been putrid at keeping opponents out of scoring position and the end zone this season. On the other side, Georgia defense has been dominated by power run concepts, so Baugh should find a way to put Florida on the board. Jones is also an X-factor, as offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner will have an expanded playbook for the sophomore and starter Aaron Philo. The SEC showdown moves from Jacksonville for the first time in decades, with significant postseason implications hanging in the balance. The Gators sit at No. 20 on the US LBM Coaches Poll , while the Bulldogs land at No. 3. Both teams entered their bye weeks under very different circumstances. Georgia surrendered its perfect record after being upset by Auburn and Florida knocked off Texas on the road to end a two-game skid. Under first-year head coach Jon Sumrall, the Gators have demonstrated an ability to compete with elite programs. However, inconsistency and sporadic lapses in execution paint question marks around UF's ceiling this season. Florida will need star running back Jadan Baugh to get going early to establish offensive balance and open up the play sheet for lead coordinator Buster Faulkner. Georgia boasts the No. 1 total defense in the SEC, so the Gators will need to stay out of predictable situations to maximize their weapons. The Gators' pass rush will need to recreate the pressure it delivered in Austin when the group sacked Arch Manning five times and forced two fumbles. Gunner Stockon turned the ball over three times against Auburn, so the opportunities should be there for Brad White's unit. Florida is again in the midst of a quarterback controversy. Aaron Philo led the Gators to a 4-0 start and was a driving force in their upset win over No. 4 Ole Miss in the Swamp before being sidelined by a right shoulder injury. In his first career start, Tramell Jones Jr. completed 22 of 35 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns in a win over Texas that revived the Gators' season. Sumrall has yet to announce a starter as of Wednesday afternoon. Led by Gunner Stockton, Georgia's offense averages 43 points per game; a scoring attack that ranks No. 3 nationally. home.blurb: When Georgia football star safety KJ Bolden was out for the Auburn game, the Bulldogs turned to Ja'Marley Riddle to step up in his place. Part of the reason, coach Kirby Smart indicated Wednesday, is Jones is still dealing with a foot injury that kept him out the last eight games of the 2025 season. The Charlotte native is in his fourth season with Georgia . Smart said that outside linebacker Amaris Williams, the Auburn transfer who sustained a torn ACL in the spring, is doing limited work in practice. Smart said he did not know now if Williams could possibly return to play this season. home.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
home.blurb: Kirby Smart detailed on Monday how Georgia handled their bye week differently this season. In the past they have continued to practice like normal with limited time off, but this year they only practiced on Tuesday and Thursday and had the rest of the week off. "Really don't know on either one of them because we haven't done anything since Thursday,” Kirby Smart said via 247Sports.com . “Those guys, we had good practices all week last week, and then leading into this week, we'll find out more about where they are today and through the injury report information we have.” Smart made it clear that he is willing to sacrifice some practice time to get his team healthy. In fact, this is something that Georgia has been doing all season because they have shortened each of their practices all season by 10 or 15 minutes. The goal in this is to help Georgia stay healthier without giving up too much preparation time, and so far it has worked out alright. The hope though is that guys like Isiah Canion and KJ Bolden could use this extra time off this week to get healthy so they can make their return against Florida this weekend, but Smart hasn't confirmed if they will be back yet or not. The hope is that this would help get Georgia as healthy as possible going into the rest of the season, but according to Smart on Monday it still isn't clear if wide receiver Isiah Canion or defensive back KJ Bolden will be healthy enough to play against Florida this weekend. picks.blurb: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road Skip to main content SI.COM Olympic Sports More from Northwestern Wildcats On SI FOOTBALL The Wildcats hit the road once again, this time traveling west to Eugene, Oregon, for a Big Ten showdown against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT. Oregon enters Saturday’s matchup looking to bounce back following a 21-10 loss to Illinois. The Ducks have been without starting quarterback Dante Moore for the past three games, and recent reports indicate he is unlikely to return this season after suffering a concussion earlier this year against USC. Oregon now sits at 10th in the conference with a 4-3 overall record this season. Meanwhile, the Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup fresh off a commanding 42-14 home victory over Rutgers, a win that propelled Northwestern to No. 20 in the AP Poll. A familiar face will return to Eugene this weekend, as former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly will take on the Ducks, this time as the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator. Under Kelly’s leadership, Northwestern’s offense has emerged as one of the best in the Big Ten this season, ranking third in the conference in total yards and points per game and second in rushing yards per game. The Wildcats head to Eugene looking to build on their success on both sides of the ball and extend their four-game winning streak. A major contributor to Northwestern’s offensive success this season has been quarterback Aidan Chiles, this week’s Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week, who has thrown for over 1,600 yards and 12 touchdowns, while recording just one interception. Chiles was dominant last time out against Rutgers, throwing for 219 yards and passing for three touchdowns, while rushing for 83 yards and two touchdowns. Komolafe delivered an especially impressive performance against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats’ convincing victory. Defensively, Northwestern has remained stout this season, spearheaded by defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and line backer Braydon Brus. Despite missing the last two games due to injury, Fitzgerald has recorded 49 tackles and two interceptions this season. Brus leads the defensive unit with 62 tackles and has also notched an interception and fumble recovery this season. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football takes on Northwestern Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 28, 2026, 8:52 a.m. PT Oregon's national-title hopes have ended after a loss to Illinois dropped them to 4-3. Oregon will face a one-loss Northwestern team featuring former Ducks coach Chip Kelly as offensive coordinator. The Ducks' defense is expected to play well, but the offense faces a tough challenge against Northwestern. The Oregon football team's national title hopes are all but over, and it isn't even November. After entering the season ranked as high as they've ever been, the Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) are unranked and out of the immediate College Football Playoff race after a stunning loss to Illinois on the road . The Ducks don't have much time to lick their wounds, either. After firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and announcing quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the 2026 season , one-loss Northwestern comes to town . Chip Kelly, who guided Oregon to a national championship game appearance as head coach over a decade ago, is the Wildcats' offensive coordinator. "It's almost like you're playing three different offenses," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said of Northwestern. "The new wrinkles that (Kelly) has at Northwestern, some of the old flavor that he has that he's carried all the way to his time back here at Oregon. There's always going to be something new when you walk into a game that it's going to be like he's never put this on film. He might not know how you're going to line up against it, and you have to figure it out there within the rules of your defense and how you execute." Oregon vs. Northwestern scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks will have the home crowd behind them in Eugene and also have deep familiarity with Northwestern's starting quarterback, Aidan Chiles. The senior signal-caller started his career at Oregon State before transferring to Michigan State in 2024. Chiles played at Autzen Stadium in that year and had a rough outing, completely just 10 of 17 passes for 154 yards in a 31-10 loss. The Ducks found ways to rattle Chiles early, and with a strong pass rush in recent weeks they could do so again Saturday. Why Northwestern has an advantage: The Wildcats, under first-year offensive coordinator and former Ducks coach Chip Kelly, have one of the most efficient offenses in the country and don't make many mistakes. Northwestern isn't necessarily an offensive juggernaut, but it ranks fifth in the country in turnover margin and moves the ball methodically while keeping opposing teams out of the end zone defensively. Though the Wildcats' defense gives up plenty of yards, they rank in the top 25 in scoring defense allowing just 16.6 points per game. Oregon vs. Northwestern injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: The Ducks will have a good chunk of playmakers returning to the sideline this weekend after sitting out last week due to unknown reasons. Evan Stewart, who was out last week after a DUII arrest, is expected back, as are Jalen Lott and Messiah Hampton. Lanning did not elaborate why Hampton and Lott missed last week. The coach also announced quarterback Dante Moore will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season after sustaining a concussion in late September. For Northwestern: The Wildcats were without several key contributors last week in a win against Rutgers, especially defensively. Second-leading tackler Robert Fitzgerald was held out, as well as defensive lineman Brendan Flakes. Oregon vs. Northwestern: 4 bold predictions Ducks will mostly contain vaunted Northwestern run game Though Chiles has been successful through the air in recent weeks, Northwestern's bread and butter is establishing the ground game. After a subpar performance stopping the run last week against Illinois, Oregon's defense will show up ready to play and stifle backs Caleb Komolafe, Joseph Himon II and Gavin Sawchuk. Outside of games versus Oklahoma State and Illinois, Oregon's run defense has been sound and it'll look like a motivated group against a physical Wildcats team this weekend. Gage Hurych will have a bounce-back performance vs. Wildcats After missing three field goals last week in a loss to Illinois, all from 40 yards or more, junior kicker Gage Hurych will have a strong game against Northwestern. The Wildcats give up a lot of yards with a bend-but-don't-break defense but are elite in the red zone, an area where Oregon's offense struggles. Northwestern opponents only score a touchdown on 40% of possessions that reach the red zone. If Oregon's offense stalls as it gets closer to the end zone, look for Hurych to have a bounce-back performance with more manageable field-goal attempts. Ducks' defense will keep them in it until the end Though Oregon's offense will likely still have trouble after firing Drew Mehringer, its defense will respond and keep them in the game until the fourth quarter. Outside of a couple of broken off runs in a loss to Illinois, the Ducks' defense has been one of the top units in the country over the last month and that will continue against Northwestern this weekend. It just won't be enough to get a win, unless the offense really corrects itself. picks.headline: Northwestern is up next for Oregon football. A sneak preview
picks.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Northwestern is up next for Oregon football. A sneak preview Chris Hansen Eugene Register-Guard Oct. 26, 2026, 5:14 a.m. PT The Oregon Ducks will host the No. 18 Northwestern Wildcats on Saturday, October 31. Northwestern's offense is led by former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly, who is now the offensive coordinator. Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles is having a career-best season under Kelly's guidance. No time to wallow for Oregon's coaches and players. There's still lots of football left and against some pretty good teams. That includes this coming weekend. The Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten Conference) will host No. 18 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) and former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly at 12:30 p.m. Oct. 31. Kelly, who is in his first season as offensive coordinator on coach David Braun's staff, has the Wildcats humming. They are third in the Big Ten in total yards per game (435.6) and points (34.7) and are No. 2 in rushing yards per game (204.6). Northwestern is coming off a 42-14 win against Rutgers, the fourth straight win for the Wildcats since a 29-23 loss to Indiana on Sept. 25. The Ducks are coming off a 21-10 loss to Illinois that, barring a miracle, has ended their shot at making the College Football Playoff for a third straight season. On Sunday, Oregon fired first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . Here's an early look at Northwestern. Who is the Northwestern QB? The Wildcats have a familiar face at quarterback in Aidan Chiles, who previously played at Oregon State and Michigan State. The 6-foot-4, 225-pound dual-threat senior has been unlocked by Kelly and is having the best season of his career. Chiles has completed 117 of 164 passes for 1,617 yards and has 12 touchdowns to one interception. He's also rushed for a team-leading nine touchdowns. Last week against Rutgers he completed 19 of 25 passes for 219 yards and three touchdowns and rushed for 83 yards and two touchdowns. He is the only player in the country to have multiple games of at least three passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns this season. Other Northwestern offensive standouts Junior wide receiver Griffin Wilde has 39 catches for 615 yards and four touchdowns. In the game against Rutgers on Saturday, he had nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown. Running back Caleb Komolafe leads the Wildcats in rushing with 551 yards and five touchdowns on 88 carries. He also had a big game against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown on just 13 carries (11.5 yards per run). Joseph Himon II has been productive as well. He has 371 yards and three scores on 38 carries with an average of 9.8 yards per run. Defensive standouts for Northwestern Fifth-year Braydon Brus has been disruptive from his linebacker position, leading the team with 62 tackles, 11.0 tackles for loss and four sacks. He also has an interception and a fumble recovery. He is the conference co-leader in tackles and No. 2 in TFLs. Safety Robert Fitzgerald, a second-team all-conference player in 2025, is second on the team with 49 tackles and has a team-leading two interceptions, though he has missed the last two games with an injury. Fitzgerald’s 9.0 tackles per game leads the Big Ten. The last time the Ducks and Wildcats met Oregon and Northwestern have played each other just two times, and never before at Autzen Stadium. The Wildcats beat the Ducks in Evanston, Ill., in 1974, and last season Oregon came out on top 34-14. Dante Moore was 16-of-20 passing for 178 yards and a touchdown, and Dierre Hill Jr. had a 66-yard touchdown run in the third quarter as the Ducks built a 31-0 lead. All of Northwestern's points came in the fourth quarter after the Ducks pulled most of their starters. home.headline: Chip Kelly returns to Eugene as Northwestern faces struggling Oregon
home.blurb: “I kind of described before, it’s almost like you’re playing three different offenses with the new wrinkles that he has in Northwestern, some of the old flavor that he’s carried all the way to his time back here at Oregon,” Lanning said. “And then there’s always gonna be something new when you walk into a game that it’s gonna be like, he’s never put this on film. He might not know how you’re gonna line up against it. And you have to figure it out there within the rules of your defense, and how you execute.” EUGENE — Chip Kelly is coming back to Oregon . Not as the Ducks’ new offensive coordinator. At least not yet, should Dan Lanning pursue that reunion this offseason. At the helm of a dynamic Northwestern offense, Kelly comes to town on Saturday seeking his first win at Autzen Stadium since he hung up his white and green visor in 2012. It is perhaps his best opportunity: The surging Wildcats are 6-1 (3-1 Big Ten), and the Ducks (4-3, 2-2) are reeling after a 21-10 loss to Illinois last week — after which they fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and announced quarterback Dante Moore is done for the season . “They’re playing complete football,” Oregon coach Dan Lanning said of Northwestern. “What they do on offense, it’s almost like they have three different offenses. And the way they operate, they’re running the ball extremely effectively. Their quarterback is playing at a really, really high level, extremely efficient.” The Wildcats boast the No. 35 scoring offense in the country at 35.7 points per game, ranked No. 23 in rushing yards per game at 204.6. Quarterback Aidan Chiles is on pace for by far the best season of a career that also spans Oregon State and Michigan State, completing 71.3% of his passes for 1,617 yards, 12 touchdowns and one interception. He’s also rushed for 181 yards and nine touchdowns. Oregon’s defense has found its stride in recent weeks, despite the Ducks’ offensive ineptitude. But Chris Hampton’s group will still have its hands full with this Northwestern side. “I think the great thing about Chip is he always does an unbelievable job utilizing his personnel and finding things that they do at a really high level,” Lanning said. “So, there’s things you’re seeing in Northwestern now that they haven’t done in the past, anywhere that he’s been. And then there’s wrinkles that are like, okay, that’s a Chip play, that’s an identity play that he’s kind of always carried..” Kelly has put this team in position to succeed time and again this season, running an array of dizzying formations from the Wing-T to unconventional versions of the spread. After winning a national title in 2024 as the offensive coordinator for Ohio State, he spent one season with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025 before returning to college football with the retooled Wildcats. picks.blurb: South Carolina vs. Oklahoma Preview: Gamecocks Look to Extend Winning Streak in Norman - SEC Country Skip to content Alabama Mississippi State South Carolina Instagram X-twitter Youtube Search Search Shop Alabama Stephan Stroud October 28, 2026 The South Carolina Gamecocks travel to Norman this weekend for a critical SEC showdown against the Oklahoma Sooners, with both programs looking to build momentum as the regular season enters its second half. South Carolina enters Saturday’s matchup at 4-3 overall and 2-3 in SEC play after earning consecutive victories over ranked opponents Florida and Tennessee. Oklahoma is also 4-3, sitting at 2-2 in conference play after defeating Mississippi State 23-15 last weekend. With both teams searching for consistency, Saturday’s matchup could have major implications for their postseason hopes. Shane Beamer and South Carolina Seek Another Statement Win Head coach Shane Beamer has watched his Gamecocks respond impressively after a difficult stretch earlier in the season. South Carolina dropped three consecutive games against Mississippi State, Alabama and Kentucky before bouncing back with its victory over Florida. Latest episode SEC Country Podcast New shows Monday & Wednesday Airing It Out with Aaron Murray · Oct 28 Quarterback LaNorris Sellers remains the centerpiece of South Carolina’s offense. Sellers has thrown for 1,548 yards, 13 touchdowns and five interceptions this season while adding 507 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns. His dual-threat ability makes him dangerous against any defense. Against Tennessee, Sellers completed 18 of 32 passes for 210 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 96 yards and two scores. However, Oklahoma presents a significant challenge. The Sooners have one of the nation’s strongest defenses, and Sellers will need to make smart decisions while taking advantage of opportunities to extend plays with his legs. Beamer will also look for his defense, led by standout pass rusher Dylan Stewart, to pressure Oklahoma’s quarterback and force mistakes. Brent Venables and the Sooners Look for Consistency Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables enters this matchup hoping his team can finally put together consecutive victories. The Sooners have alternated wins and losses throughout the season, making Saturday an important opportunity to establish momentum. Quarterback John Mateer leads the Oklahoma offense. He has thrown for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns, although seven interceptions have created challenges for the Sooners. Mateer showed encouraging signs during Oklahoma’s 23-15 victory over Mississippi State. The Sooners recorded a season high 467 total yards and rushed for 184 yards, giving their offense a much-needed boost. Getting left tackle Michael Fasusi back from injury helped stabilize the offensive line, although additional injuries remain a concern. Oklahoma will need to protect Mateer against South Carolina’s aggressive pass rush. Venables’ defense could ultimately determine the outcome. The Sooners have been particularly effective against opposing passing attacks, using pressure and complicated defensive schemes to disrupt quarterbacks. Key Matchups to Watch The biggest battle will be Sellers against Oklahoma’s defense. If South Carolina’s quarterback can create plays with his arm and legs, the Gamecocks have a chance to control the game. Meanwhile, Mateer must protect the football and take advantage of scoring opportunities against a South Carolina defense coming off an impressive second-half performance against Tennessee. Special teams and turnovers could also prove decisive in what should be a competitive SEC contest. Final Thoughts South Carolina enters with confidence after two consecutive victories, but winning on the road against Oklahoma will be another major test for Beamer’s team. Venables and the Sooners will be motivated to defend their home field and establish a winning streak of their own. Kickoff is scheduled for Saturday, October 31, at 4:15 p.m. ET on the SEC Network. With two teams looking to strengthen their seasons, this matchup has the potential to deliver another compelling chapter in SEC football. away.headline: No. 11 Tennessee vs. South Carolina injury report: Vols, Gamecocks final availability
away.blurb: For the Gamecocks, defensive back Quay’sheed Scott was ruled out in Friday’s availability report. Scott has nine tackles this season, including one for loss. Offensive lineman Carter Miller, who has missed the last two games for South Carolina, is no longer on the report and is available. Running back Jawarn Howell has been ruled out. The Southeastern Conference has released its final availability report for No. 11 Tennessee’s game at South Carolina . For the Vols, no players have been added to the report other than the six who were lost for the season earlier this year: Tennessee will head into the game as an underdog despite its No. 11 national ranking. Head coach Josh Heupel preached fundamentals and preparation this week. “I’ve said it to our football team, I think I’ve said it here a couple times, every week’s a new season inside of this league. That’s whether you’re playing at home or on the road, you’ve got to play,” Heupel said Monday. “The margins are just, they’re small, they’re tight. A play here, a call there, can make a huge difference. So, you’ve got to be on the right side of it in your preparation.” Below is the full South Carolina availability report: No. 11 Tennessee and South Carolina are set for 3:30 p.m. ET at Williams-Brice Stadium. The game will be televised on ESPN, with Wes Durham (play-by-play) and Dusty Dvoracek (analyst) on the call. Taylor McGregor will have the sideline report. away.headline: South Carolina vs. Tennessee football: Kickoff time, TV channel, injury report, odds
away.blurb: The sportsbooks out in Vegas have had a change of heart on this game in recent days. WR Jayden Sellers, EDGE Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josiah Thompson and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Thompson and Sellers are both out for the year. Two starters are listed on the report in DB Quay’sheed Scott and OL Carter Miller. Scott is listed as doubtful and Miller is listed as questionable. Both missed the Florida game. Run vs. run: Saturday’s matchup will feature the two best rushing offenses in the SEC . South Carolina is No. 1 in the league with 232.33 yards per game and Tennessee is No. 2 in the league with 217.14 yards per game. Both have star running backs — Matt Fuller for USC and DeSean Bishop for Tennessee — and strong offensive lines. USC’s rushing attack was weaker than usual last time out against Florida, and will need to get back to its usual ways if it wants to outrun the Vols. Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks will face No. 11 Tennessee at Williams-Brice Stadium on Saturday. The SEC matchup is set to kick off at 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on ESPN. South Carolina (3-3, 1-3 SEC) is coming off a bye week but knocked off ranked Florida on the road for its first SEC win on the road on Oct. 10. Tennessee (6-1, 3-1 SEC) enters Saturday’s matchup ranked No. 11 in the country after beating rival Alabama last week. Tennessee leads the all-time series against South Carolina 29-11-2. The Volunteers beat the Gamecocks 41-20 in 2023, the last time the two teams faced each other. South Carolina rolled to a 63-38 win over Tennessee in 2022, the last time the two teams played in Columbia. From 2012-2020, eight of the nine matchups between the SEC rivals were decided by six or fewer points. Each of the last three games have been decided by double-digit margins. home.headline: Mississippi State football vs Oklahoma prediction as Kamario Taylor injury status looms
home.blurb: The outcome of this game hinges a lot on Taylor's injury status. He was listed as questionable on the initial SEC availability report. If he plays, especially if he's close to the superstar level he was at the first four games of the season, Mississippi State should feel good about its chances to win. If Taylor is out again, it will be much more difficult for MSU to win. QB Kamario Taylor: Questionable RB Fluff Bothwell: Questionable LB Zakari Tillman: Questionable WR Parker Livingstone: Questionable RB Xavier Robinson: Questionable OL Michael Fasusi: Questionable STARKVILLE — Mississippi State football is in need of a rebound after back-to-back lopsided losses. The Bulldogs (4-2, 2-2 SEC) are hosting Oklahoma (3-3, 1-2) at Davis Wade Stadium on Oct. 24 (2:30 p.m., SEC Network). It's the first time MSU coach Jeff Lebby is facing his former team as a head coach. Mississippi State lost, 56-23, against Alabama in Week 5 with star quarterback Kamario Taylor unable to finish the game because of an injury. Then after an open date, Mississippi State lost, 31-0 at LSU without Taylor and starting running back Fluff Bothwell. Here is our score prediction for the game. Buy Mississippi State vs Oklahoma tickets Mississippi State vs Oklahoma prediction This could be a low-scoring game, even if Taylor plays. Oklahoma's strength is its defense that ranks sixth in the SEC with 18.2 points per game. Offensively, Oklahoma is 15th in the SEC with 21.3 points per game. Billy Puckett would be making his second career start if Taylor doesn't play. The former walk-on from Jackson Prep led Mississippi State to 291 yards against LSU but no points with a 0-for-5 mark on fourth down. Puckett went 16-for-26 with 121 passing yards, no touchdowns, one interception and 40 rushing yards. John Mateer is Oklahoma's second-year quarterback and has thrown for 1,308 yards, nine touchdowns and seven interceptions. Oklahoma has dealt with injuries at offensive line that Mississippi State could benefit from. home.headline: Oklahoma OT Michael Fasusi Expected to Return Against Mississippi State
home.blurb: Michael Fasusi was not listed on the final availability report ahead of OU's matchup against Mississippi State . He is projected to return to his starting spot at left tackle. The talented left tackle, who has missed every game since the Sooners' opener against UTEP, where he played only 17 snaps on offense per Pro Football Focus, was replaced by Ryan Fodje in OU's second game against Michigan. Fodje held the position over the next few weeks until his injury in last week's loss to Kentucky. Fodje is listed as out for today's game. Fasusi was initially listed as questionable on the SEC availability report on Wednesday. He was never upgraded on the Thursday and Friday reports. Eddy Pierre-Louis , a captain and starting left guard, has been out since appearing on the SEC availability report the week of the Texas game. He was in a cast on his right leg and used a single walking crutch. Pierre-Louis also missed last week's game against Kentucky and is out for today's game. Guard Heath Ozaeta was also not listed on the final availability report heading into the game with Mississippi State , meaning he will be available for the contest. Ozaeta appeared to injure his ankle during pregame warm-ups at the Cotton Bowl, but was able to play the entire game. Ozaeta missed last week and has been listed as questionable on this week's SEC availability reports. If he's available, he is projected to start at right guard. STARKVILLE, Miss. — Oklahoma's offensive line is getting a massive reinforcement. Per Sooners on SI sources, Fasusi has practiced all week to prepare for the start. He has slowly ramped up his availability over the last few weeks as he deals with a right shoulder injury. In that game against UTEP, Fasusi was visibly dealing with the injury he sustained in Fall Camp. In his 17 offensive snaps, Fasusi was unable to lift or use his right arm in his final opportunities. Fasusi is a welcome addition to a depleted unit that has regressed both due to injuries and a lack of development. Fasusi could play alongside Noah Best , Jake Maikkula , and E'Marion Harris . If Ozaeta is unable to finish the game, he could be replaced by Peyton Joseph, who logged 69 offensive snaps in his first start of the season at right guard last week. home.headline: Rapid Reaction: Oklahoma Sooners beat Mississippi State 23-15
home.blurb: Isaiah Sategna led the receiving corps with eight receptions for 164 yards and a touchdown. His second-half touchdown seemed to spark the Sooners' offense coming out of halftime. FINAL: Oklahoma Sooners close out win, 23-15 The Oklahoma Sooners got the ball back with just over two minutes to play and John Mateer came through on a pair of critical third downs. First, running and diving for the first down to open the drive. Then, on third-and-11, Mateer rolled out and hit Beers for a 13-yard completion to get the final first down, allowing the Sooners to kneel the ball and close out the win. The Sooners defense has played great for most of the game but it's going to be on the offense to go close it out under two minutes. John Mateer hit Isaiah Sategna for a big play and the Oklahoma Sooners looked like they had a touchdown when Mateer hit Beers in the end zone, but the ball was knocked out of his hands late, after the play seemed dead, and the referees deemed it incomplete. Tate Sandell kicked his second field goal of the game to make it 20-7. The Oklahoma Sooners got the ball back after a punt and were moving out of their own end of the field after a couple of first downs. Mateer hit Rocky Beers for a big gain, but when Beers tried to hurdle the defender, the ball came out and was recovered by Mississippi State. Explosive out of the half: Sooners lead 17-0 - 13:44, third quarter The Oklahoma Sooners went three-and-out for the first time today. Mateer hit Hayden Hansen on second down and hit Jonathan Hatton on the dump-off on third down but was tackled short of the first-down marker. Mississippi State broke into Sooners' territory on a big run from Fluff Bothwell. But that's all they could muster on the drive. A deep ball to Anthony Evans was just out of his reach and Reggie Powers III stopped Evans for a loss on a wide receiver screen. On fourth-and-6, Kamario Taylor attempted to break out of the pocket and pick up the yardage with his legs, but came up hobbling due to the turf toe injury on his right foot. Owen Heinecke was able to run him to the sideline for the sack and turnover on downs. For the first time since Week 1, projected starting left tackle Michael Fasusi will be available for the Oklahoma Sooners. With Ryan Fodje, who started the last five games at left tackle ruled out earlier in the week, expect Fasusi to return to his spot on John Mateer's blindside. Guard Heath Ozaeta is also available to play this week. He could take back his spot at right guard, where he started in the Sooners' win over Texas. Peyton Joseph could also start at guard again. Starting corner Eli Bowen and starting wide receiver Elijah Thomas will be out for this week as well, meaning Trystan Haynes will make his third consecutive start since taking over before the Texas game.
