home.headline: Oklahoma leads SEC in players out, doubtful or questionable on Thursday injury report
home.blurb: Oklahoma leads SEC in players out, doubtful or questionable on Thursday injury report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF As of Wednesday's initial report, the Sooners had more players out, doubtful and questionable -- 13 -- than any other SEC team. Vanderbilt had 11 and Ole Miss and Alabama had 10 on those lists. On Thursday, it wasn't much better. Oklahoma had 11 players listed as out, doubtful or questionable. Ole Miss had 10 and Alabama, Mississippi State and Vanderbilt had nine. The issue is particularly alarming on the Sooners' offensive line. As of Thursday, Eddy Pierre-Louis and Ryan Fodje were listed as out and Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta were listed as questionable. That report did not include Sean Hutton, who reportedly was transported to a local hospital Wednesday after suffering a non-contact injury . The receiver position has been hit hard, too. Trell Harris is out, and Elijah Thomas is questionable. Parker Livingstone has been upgraded to probable. Even coach Brent Venables has been out of action. He was ill and missed this week's media session. MORE: Oklahoma assistants Arbuckle, Bedenbaugh running out of time to fix offense Oklahoma offensive line coach Bedenbaugh's unit gets called out Cliff Brunt Thu, October 22, 2026 at 7:47 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Oklahoma's Southeastern Conference injury report looks like a mini roster. The injury barrage is a key reason the Sooners are just 3-3 heading into Saturday's game at Mississippi State. Venables has been asked about the injuries several times this season. "I don't track what we what we do compared to other people," he said during the week before last Saturday's loss to Kentucky. "Certainly, you're always aware that injuries are part of game, and it's a physical, violent game." Venables said the team has to practice hard to be successful, so tapering back to avoid injury is not an option. "If you're casual at practice, you don't strain to finish at practice, all of those habits, good or bad, are going to show up," he said. "There's always a fine line. We've got to keep a healthy team, but we're very mindful of the time we put on the field, wear our GPS stuff, we look at all those types of things as well." Venables said much of the issue is coincidental, and he doesn't think there's anything fundamentally wrong with the way the team prepares. "We're not doing things different from how I've done it for a long time, whether I was an assistant or not," he said. "We have to practice the right way, though." home.headline: Sooners still list three players questionable on Friday injury report
home.blurb: Offensive linemen Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta and defensive back Eli Bowen were all listed as questionable on Friday night. Getting Fasusi and Ozaeta back would be a big boost for the o-line, while a return for Bowen would put the secondary back nearer to full strength than its been in weeks. That trio will be the players to watch on the final injury report on Saturday. The good news for the Sooners is that running back Tory Blaylock and wide receiver Parker Livingstone are off the injury report and therefore available to play in Starkville this week. Blaylock's return gives the Sooners a three-man rotation in the backfield again, while Livingstone's return gives them another option in the passing game. However, the Sooners also downgraded wide receiver Elijah Thomas to doubtful on Friday, meaning he likely won't face the Bulldogs. Running back Xavier Robinson will be out once again, as he was downgraded from doubtful to out. Along with Robinson, the Sooners will also not have wide receiver Trell Harris, tight end Trynae Washington, offensive linemen Eddy Pierre-Louis and Ryan Fodje, linebacker Taylor Heim, and defensive back Jacobe Johnson on Saturday. For Mississippi State, they got good news with the return of star running back Fluff Bothwell, who is off the injury report and is expected to play. According to multiple reports , star quarterback Kamario Taylor is also going to play this week, despite still being listed as questionable on Friday night's report. That means the Bulldogs will be getting their two best players back on the offensive side of the ball for Saturday's game. However, MSU will not have safety Issac Smith, which will be a big blow to their defense this week. Here's a look at Friday night's full injury report. picks.headline: ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Florida State
picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, doesn't favor the Tigers, either. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. Florida State has a 10.1 FPI rating that's 37th nationally. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Kansas State (5.7) and one spot below Virginia (6.0). picks.blurb: Early odds for Florida State vs. Clemson in Week 9 show what standing with Miami can do Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball & softball FanSided NCAA Sites After battling through injuries and adversity against Miami in Week 7, Florida State must now return to the playing field against the Clemson Tigers. Week 7 was exhausting for everyone, between the gritty battle on the field, the two ridiculous calls, and the season-ending injury to star running back Ousmane Kromah. Even with a bye in Week 8, the tension from the previous weeks feels like it is lingering, and the Seminoles now need to get back into the win column. Florida State's first opponent after the bye week will be Clemson, a team sitting in a very similar position with little success on the field despite very high expectations. Coach Mike Norvell is going to be sticking around Tallahassee for a bit longer, and losing to Clemson directly after that announcement became public would be an awful look. Norvell may not have secured the win in Coral Gables, but taking Miami into double overtime appears to have been enough to win back the trust of the public. After previously hosting Virginia this season as underdogs, Florida State is a home favorite for the first time since hosting Central Arkansas earlier in the year. The Seminoles should be favorites at home games with the crowd that the team can bring in, but, notably, Florida State is a heavier moneyline favorite than normal. The last time Florida State played at home this season, Virginia was considered to be the favorite despite being the visiting team. The Seminoles impressed with a dominant win, but now the team needs to same result on the field with the public backing them this time. There is enough evidence to suggest this can be a strong team, but consistency has been the problem the Seminoles cannot shake. Clemson is not coming into the game as the hottest team either, which could factor into the support for Florida State. The Tigers are 4-3, and with no real solution at quarterback, the team does not look like one that can muster up enough offense to beat opponents. Clemson has scored 29 points in the last two ACC games against Virginia Tech and Miami after posting 52 in the first two conference games. The Tigers averaged 4.6 yards per play during the 41-13 loss to Miami, with quarterback Tait Reynolds turning the ball over twice. The offense managed to move the ball against a solid Virginia Tech defense, but the team still only put together a 16-point performance, which will not be enough to defeat Florida State. Losing to Miami definitely stings, but the reality is that the ACC as a whole is not that great this season outside of the Hurricanes, SMU, and Wake Forest. Florida State could definitely take advantage of that moving forward with similar performances on offense to the one that brought the team into double overtime. away.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
away.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' away.headline: Two FSU freshmen trending toward returning vs. Clemson
away.blurb: Crutchfield has been in and out of FSU's lineup this season as he battles injuries, but the coaching staff has been extremely pleased with what he can do, and Norvell is "hopeful" he will be available this week. "I think Jordan Crutchfield is trending well to be able to get back in the secondary," Norvell said. "We've had some guys that have been banged up there as well. Jordan's a guy that has shown some flashes here, just dealt with some minor injuries that have kind of set him back just from the consistency of his opportunities, but expecting him to get some good work here this week and hopefully be available." The update was less positive about Nichelson, who hasn't played since the game against the New Mexico State Aggies, and Norvell doesn't expect that to change this week. He is "hopeful" that the rest of the linebackers will be able to play after several were in and out of the Miami game with injuries. Head coach Mike Norvell spoke with the media on Monday and provided an injury update ahead of Saturday's game against the Clemson Tigers , specifically mentioning freshman wide receiver Devin Carter, linebacker Blake Nichelson, and freshman defensive back Jordan Crutchfield. Carter, who the coaching staff praised all offseason, has not played this season after hurting his back and ribs during the preseason. That could be changing soon, per Norvell. "Devin Carter is coming into having an opportunity this week, barring any setbacks, we'll see where that goes," Norvell said. "You'll see what that looks like, another explosive player that brings opportunity." home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. home.blurb: Florida State could receive a massive boost on defense with Blake Nichelson nearing a return Skip to main content Recruiting Coach Mike Norvell took the podium this afternoon following practice for his first press conference of the week, and some injury updates were provided. Norvell revealed that senior linebacker Blake Nichelson is "progressing" but likely still would not be able to return to play just yet. With Clemson coming to Tallahassee on October 31, Nichelson may need more time to properly rehab his injury. The linebacker recorded three total tackles against New Mexico State in the season opener in Tallahassee before going down with an injury. Nichelson has not seen the field since, but a return during the season has never been ruled out. Florida State could greatly benefit from a Blake Nichelson return this season Both for Nichelson and Florida State, returning to the field this season would be extremely beneficial, given the struggles the team has had. The Seminoles are down so many players at some positions that some players are playing significantly more than the staff would like. Nichelson gives the rest of the linebackers a chance to breathe, and he offers the staff a veteran presence that can help the defense work out some of the communication issues present. Florida State is right back into game mode after receiving a bye in Week 8 to recuperate for the final five games of the 2026 season. The year has been far from what the fans had hoped for, but unfortunately, it has been eerily similar to what many experts felt it would be. Once again, the Seminoles are in an awkward position as the light that comes with winning is slowly fading away. For the Seminoles, virtually the entire roster has been hit with injuries at one point or another this season, and some positions took big hits. The secondary has been running with nearly no depth due to the number of injuries, and other positions have been playing without key players for most of the season. At linebacker, Nichelson was expected to take another step forward this season for Florida State, with a bigger role on defense. However, Nichelson's injury forced the Seminoles' staff to move things around, and nearly every linebacker has been included in an injury report this season. The Seminoles need to get healthy to be more competitive this season, and getting Nichelson back would be a huge boost defensively. Nichelson has been a Florida State mainstay the past few seasons , with 115 total tackles since the 2023 season. Losing Nichelson so early on in the season was an unfortunate blow, as what should have been a breakout season for the linebacker has turned into a disappointing year. home.blurb: Injuries to running backs Ousmane Kromah and Samuel Singleton Jr. have dismantled the Seminoles' backfield, but there might be a different way to ignite the offense moving forward. Senior wide receiver Duce Robinson has been relatively quiet this season, and Florida State needs that to change with much of the bite of the rushing attack out of the equation. Florida State needs Duce Robinson to step up after serious injuries on offense Skip to main content Recruiting With the bye week now behind them, Florida State will launch straight into full preparation for the Week 9 clash against the Clemson Tigers. The Seminoles fought hard in Week 7 against Miami, taking them into double overtime, but ultimately, there was not quite enough done to secure what would have been a monster upset. The Seminoles have no time to live in the past, with just five games remaining before the end of the regular season. Florida State needs to pull off an improbable winning streak to qualify for a bowl game for the first time since the 2023 season. The Florida State offense may need Duce Robinson now more than ever Robinson joined the team ahead of the 2025 season after two somewhat productive seasons with the USC Trojans. Last season with Florida State, Robinson was a massive part of the offense and rightfully so with his 6-foot-6 frame. However, the receiver has not been able to take a serious step forward this season after posting 1081 yards and six touchdowns a year ago. There have been flashes this season for Robinson, particularly against Miami and Alabama, but it has been feast or famine for the receiver. Robinson recorded 11 receptions, 248 yards, and three touchdowns in those two games, and he has recorded 11 receptions, 159 yards, and one touchdown in the other five. Florida State needs to be able to attack teams through the air moving forward with just three healthy running backs, including two who have barely seen the collegiate field. The Seminoles cannot just rely on the ground game without the players who made their rushing attack special, which means someone in the receiving room needs to pick up the offense. Robinson is the most obvious candidate after a successful season last year with Florida State, and two massive performances this season that kept the team competitive. The track record is there, and the receiver has been successful this season when he is consistently being targeted. Robinson averages 18.5 yards per reception this season, and when Daniels is able to connect with his receivers, it is often for a good chunk of yards. A more consistent Robinson would be huge for Florida State moving forward, but the team also needs to find a way to continue to get Jayvan Boggs involved. Boggs is also averaging 18.5 yards per reception, but the Seminoles have rarely had both receivers heat up during the same game. You don't start 7-0, score nearly 50 points a game and climb to No. 1 by accident. But there's something about laying more than two touchdowns on the road that makes me uncomfortable, especially against a North Carolina team that's been hanging around with some decent opponents. Miami probably wins this game. I'd be surprised if it didn't. But asking the Hurricanes to go into Chapel Hill and win by 17? That's a different bet altogether. Be ready for all the college football action with our free college football picks . Miami heads to Kenan Memorial Stadium in Chapel Hill on Saturday, October 31, 2026. Kickoff is set for 7:30 PM ET on ABC. The Hurricanes opened as 14.5-point favorites, with some books now showing 15.5. Our original betting numbers were North Carolina +16.5 and Under 51.5. That extra point on the spread matters, and I wouldn't pretend every sportsbook is still offering it. This is an outdoor game, so I'll want another look at the Chapel Hill weather forecast before kickoff, particularly the wind and any chance of rain. Miami Hurricanes Have the Offense to Put This Away Early Miami is 7-0, including 3-0 away from home, and just beat Pittsburgh 52-23. The Hurricanes have scored 43 or more in three of their last four games, and they've already beaten Clemson 41-13 on the road. That's a pretty good argument for laying the points, I'll give you that. Pittsburgh couldn't do much with Miami's passing game Saturday. The Hurricanes scored 52, and the scary part is that they still left some plays out there. North Carolina isn't going to survive if it spends the first half giving Miami short fields and easy touchdowns. The numbers explain why the Hurricanes are such a big favorite. They're averaging 49 points and 552 yards per game. Nobody in the country is producing more total offense. Miami throws for about 341 yards a game and runs for another 211, so taking away one part of the offense doesn't necessarily solve anything. Defensively, the Hurricanes allow just 15.3 points and 60 rushing yards per game. Sixty. That's going to make life difficult for a North Carolina offense that hasn't run the ball particularly well. Miami also converts 54.5% of its third downs. If the Tar Heels can't get the Hurricanes off the field, that home crowd won't have much to cheer about. Sign Up Get $30 Premium Picks Credit + Exclusive Offers Darian Mensah is having one heck of a season. He's thrown for 2,151 yards with 22 touchdowns and just one interception, completing better than 81% of his passes. Against Pittsburgh, he went 31-for-37 for 387 yards and four scores. Malachi Toney caught 16 passes for 194 yards and three touchdowns in that game, giving him 952 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns on the season. Javian Mallory has added 444 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. That's plenty of offense for North Carolina to worry about. Miami does have some injuries, with receiver Jalen Moore and running back Chris Brown out for the season. Tight end Logan Gilbert is also sidelined, while Owen Ruskavich's status needs checking. But the Hurricanes haven't had much trouble scoring without them. North Carolina Tar Heels Need to Make Miami Earn Everything North Carolina is 4-3 overall and 1-2 at home. The Tar Heels had won two straight before losing 31-30 to Syracuse in overtime Saturday. That one had to sting. They had a chance to get their fifth win and instead let Syracuse walk out of Chapel Hill with it. Still, I wouldn't throw out everything North Carolina has done because of one ugly finish. The Tar Heels beat Pittsburgh 21-17 on the road and followed it with a 24-20 win at Duke. They also played Clemson to an eight-point game. Those aren't the results of a team that rolls over every time it sees a better opponent. The offense is the problem. North Carolina averages 24.4 points and 336 yards per game, and the running game produces only 114 yards a night. That's not much help against Miami's defensive front. The Tar Heels are probably going to have to throw more than they'd like. Defensively, though, they've allowed 20.9 points per game. That's respectable, even if the 373 yards they're giving up tells you opponents are moving the ball. What worries me most is third down. North Carolina allows opponents to convert 43.1% of the time. Miami is one of the best third-down teams in the country. That's a bad matchup, and Bill Belichick has to find a way to get his defense off the field before the Hurricanes start piling up possessions. Billy Edwards Jr. has thrown for 1,530 yards with 11 touchdowns and five interceptions. He passed for 271 yards and two scores against Syracuse, so he can move the ball when he gets protection. Jordan Shipp has 543 receiving yards, including eight catches for 102 yards and a touchdown Saturday. Benjamin Hall leads the running backs with 283 yards, while Demon June has seven rushing touchdowns. The Tar Heels are dealing with some injuries at receiver, including Carnell Warren and Kaden Chapman, and they're missing tight ends Jordan Washington and Jake Warren. That's not ideal when you're facing a defense as good as Miami's. But Edwards has enough experience to keep North Carolina from becoming completely one-dimensional. Miami vs North Carolina Picks and Predictions North Carolina Tar Heels +16.5 I'm taking North Carolina +16.5, assuming that number is still available. I know Miami could make this look foolish in a hurry. The Hurricanes have the better quarterback, the better offense and a defense that barely lets anybody run the ball. But sixteen and a half points is a lot to lay on the road against a team that's been competitive with Clemson, Pittsburgh and Duke. North Carolina has lost three games, and two of those defeats came by eight points or fewer. The Tar Heels also have a quarterback who can throw well enough to put together a late scoring drive if they're down a couple of touchdowns. That's what I'm looking for here. Miami can control most of the game and still fail to cover a number this big. I wouldn't be surprised by a 30-17 or 34-20 Miami win. Either one gets the job done for North Carolina backers at +16.5. At +14.5, though, I like it considerably less. I'll take Under 51.5, although this is the pick that makes me a little nervous. Miami is averaging 49 points a game by itself, and that's not something you can just ignore. But North Carolina isn't built to get into a scoring contest with the Hurricanes. The Tar Heels need to run some clock, avoid turnovers and make Miami work for its points. They can't afford to turn this into a game where both teams are snapping the ball every twenty seconds. Miami's defense should help us here because the Hurricanes allow only 15.3 points per game and have been excellent against the run. If North Carolina finishes somewhere around 14 or 17 points, Miami can score into the low 30s without pushing this over. The danger is an early Miami explosion or a couple of defensive touchdowns. That's real. But I think the Tar Heels will try to slow the game down, and Miami's defense should keep North Carolina from doing too much scoring. Give me Miami 31-17. away.headline: Notre Dame can survive its latest injury wave against Navy, but Miami is different
away.blurb: Notre Dame football’s “ next man up ” philosophy should be enough to get Marcus Freeman through Navy despite another crowded injury report. But with DJ McKinney out, Brauntae Johnson still sidelined, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa among the questionable players, Chris Ash needs that list to shrink considerably before Miami arrives. Despite the Fighting Irish coming off a bye week , head coach Marcus Freeman detailed several injuries that will hit Chris Ash’s unit hard. The good news is that none of the players who will miss time or be questionable are ones the team should need against Navy. The question is how healthy some of these guys will be in two weeks against Miami. On Monday afternoon, Freeman said McKinney is out for the Navy game with an ankle injury. That’s never good news, as that kind of injury can stick around for a while. A cornerback who can’t make cuts won’t keep up with receivers. That’s not an issue against Navy, but against Miami, especially Malachi Toney, it’s a big one. Another big injury update: safety Brauntae Johnson is still out. Notre Dame has hoped he’d be out for “just a couple of weeks” after he was injured in the first half of the season opener. However, with the season now in Week 8, people have to start worrying about whether he will play this year. The injury list doesn’t end there. Freeman said that tight end Cooper Flanagan (hamstring), linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa (thumb), defensive lineman Loghan Thomas (shoulder), and cornerback Mark Zackery IV (concussion) are all questionable. Of course, of all the injuries that might just be cautionary, KVA’s questionable status is the most likely situation where he could have been fine to play if Miami was this week. Notre Dame should absolutely be able to beat Navy even without Viliamu-Asa in the lineup. The injury that should make Notre Dame faithful most worried is DJ McKinney’s. The transfer cornerback was hurt late in the game against BYU , and the bye week apparently wasn't enough time for him to heal and get back to 100%. Notre Dame football defensive injuries create bigger questions for Miami than Navy Because Notre Dame knows Navy won’t tax its cornerbacks much, sitting McKinney this week isn’t a shock. It’s even possible that if this were Miami week , they’d be working to get him back on the field. The Irish won’t push it against the Midshipmen. The most interesting note in that group is that Notre Dame took quite a bit of heat for not playing Viliamu-Asa more against BYU. It’s clear now that one reason he wasn’t in the game more was that his thumb was still bothering him. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer return with their picks for the weekend's top games Getty Images Another weekend in college football , another carnage-filled Saturday. This feels like 2007 all over again, thanks to the pure chaos that has ensued over the last two weeks within the top 25. At this point, we're not expecting anything less on Halloween in Week 9, despite only two matchups pitting nationally ranked teams -- the SEC's Georgia vs. Florida showdown from Atlanta and Arizona vs. Texas Tech in the topsy-turvy Big 12. Only three unbeatens in the Power Four remain as the season approaches its final month, with the first CFP rankings set to debut in less than a week. We hope you're betting responsibly this fall, considering this parity-rich party nationwide that shows no signs of ceasing. Season results : Brad Crawford (47-24 straight up, 35-35-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (51-20 straight up, 38–32-1 ATS) My colleague's hot streak continues. After tying things up at midseason against the spread, Hummer's sizzling Week 8 effort has pushed him out front. It's quite humbling for yours truly, whose multi-year reign atop the picks mountain is in serious jeopardy. Perhaps Saturday afternoon comes up aces for me, and we enter November tied again after a rally. On the flip side, Hummer's could swell. No. 25 Wisconsin at Iowa (-3.5) Hummer ( Wisconsin +3.5) : These two teams do the same things well: Run the ball, stop the run. The Hawkeyes are a better rushing offense, while Wisconsin, with Colton Joseph , has the more dynamic option at quarterback -- he uses his legs a lot. To me, this game comes down to which team can avoid turnovers. They've been a killer in losses for Iowa this season. Iowa avoids those against the Badgers and wins a classic Big Ten slugfest at home. The Badgers cover, though. … Iowa 20, Wisconsin 17. Crawford (Wisconsin +3.5) : Had a feeling the Badgers would be ranked at some point this season after watching the opener against Notre Dame . The operation just looked more fluid, despite the final score in a matchup that was more competitive than the final outcome. I believe oddsmakers are giving too much respect to the Hawkeyes here playing at home. An outright win could move the Badgers inside the top 20 of the CFP selection committee's first rankings next week. I'll go ahead and take this one as my upset special in Week 9. ... Wisconsin 23, Iowa 20. No. 22 Arizona at No. 13 Texas Tech (-5.5) Hummer (Texas Tech -5.5 ): A critical matchup in the Big 12 race, the Red Raiders are facing their toughest test since Houston in Week 2. The Wildcats have put up points in bunches this season. But I will say the one week the Wildcats struggled was against BYU , when their run game was bottled up by BYU's defensive front. That's a major potential advantage for Texas Tech in this matchup. The Red Raiders are an excellent front seven and should win that matchup. Can Texas Tech score enough to win this one? It's been a struggle at times, but they get it done. … Texas Tech 27, Arizona 20. Crawford (Texas Tech -5.5) : This is the week we'll be talking about the Wildcats nationally if Arizona finds a way to beat Texas Tech in Lubbock. I don't think it happens, however. The Red Raiders' backs are against the wall in this spot, knowing another loss tanks any shot at reaching the CFP -- or even getting back to the Big 12 title game as the defending league champions. Will Hammond does not have a multi-touchdown outing this season as a passer, but this could be the weekend it finally happens at home. I trust Texas Tech more in this spot than Arizona. ... Texas Tech 31, Arizona 24. Auburn at No. 12 Ole Miss (-12.5) Hummer ( Auburn +12.5): Auburn has struggled this year against above-average defensive fronts. The Rebels aren't elite in that area, but they do blitz a ton and create a lot of havoc around the line of scrimmage. It's going to be up to Byrum Brown to pick up those blitzes and extend plays with his feet. Even without Kewan Lacy , Trinidad Chambliss allows them to score enough. The question is whether Auburn can keep up. I think the Tigers do enough to cover. … Ole Miss 34, Auburn 24. Crawford (Auburn +12.5) : Life in the SEC is hard. Auburn goes from beating Georgia in Athens one week to getting housed on The Plains by another nationally ranked foe the next. Rinse, repeat. If the Tigers had trouble defending Sam Leavitt and that LSU offense, they're going to have equally as much trouble this weekend in Oxford against Trinidad Chambliss. We've seemed to have dismissed his Heisman hopes after the loss at Texas , and that's unwise. Ole Miss gets Georgia coming up, and there are several more opportunities to shine, including this one. I do still have questions about this Ole Miss defense, however. ... Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27. Minnesota at No. 4 Indiana (-20.5) Hummer ( Minnesota +20.5) : That feels like an aggressive line based on what we've seen from Indiana 's offense of late, right? The Gophers are a top-30 defense in terms of yards allowed per play and should be able to challenge Indiana the way Nebraska , Ohio State and Michigan have in recent weeks. The question becomes, can Minnesota score enough to make this a game? The Gophers are 118th nationally in yards per play and have only scored more than 21 points against Power Four competition once this season. It's going to be tough for Minnesota to manufacture points, but the Gophers do enough. … Indiana 27, Minnesota 10. Crawford (Minnesota +20.5) : Can Indiana cover a three-touchdown spread? I have my doubts with Josh Hoover back there. Maybe this is the week the Hoosiers figure it out in the passing game, but the Gophers are sound on the back end and aren't likely to give up explosive plays. I've moved off Indiana in the elite tier of playoff contenders, but the Hoosiers should win here and be ranked inside the top 5 in next week's first CFP rankings. ... Indiana 31, Minnesota 17 . No. 17 Florida vs. No. 3 Georgia (-10.5) Hummer (Florida +10.5) : Was Florida's defensive performance against Texas an aberration or the new norm? That's the big question entering this game. The Gators are 121st nationally in passing yards per game, and the Bulldogs are a top-30 passing offense. That should be a big advantage for UGA. But that unit largely held Texas in check. Otherwise, this is a reasonably even matchup across the board. Georgia's O-line is better -- yes. Florida matches up well otherwise. Georgia wins this game coming off the bye week. But I do like the Gators to stay in this one for 60 minutes. … Georgia 34, Florida 27. Crawford (Georgia -10.5) : One of college football's most difficult teams to predict this season, I'm 0-2 picking the Gators against the spread after the loss to South Carolina and subsequent rally at Texas. I've given up trying to figure out which Florida team shows up week to week since that 4-0 start in September pushed the Gators to No. 8 in the AP poll. A victory in Atlanta puts Jon Sumrall's squad back in the CFP discussion near the top of the SEC and threatens Georgia's reign in the league standings. What's more likely, however, is Gunner Stockton recovering from his mistake-filled last outing and the Bulldogs shutting down the run. As of Tuesday, Sumrall hasn't named his starting quarterback, but I think the hotter hand -- Tramell Jones -- gives OC Buster Faulkner and the Gators the better shot here. ... Georgia 30, Florida 14. No. 6 Utah (-6.5) at Cincinnati Hummer ( Cincinnati +6.5) : On the right week, Cincinnati is capable of beating anyone in the Big 12. We just saw that against Texas Tech. But can the Bearcats do it two weeks in a row? It'll come down to the defense. That unit stepped up against the Red Raiders, holding them to 24 points. Can a unit that ranks 109th nationally in yards allowed per play do that twice in a row? I'm skeptical, especially given how good the Utes are up front. The good news for Cincinnati is its offensive line can match up with anyone. These two offensive fronts lean on each other, and the Utes pull away late. … Utah 24, Cincinnati 20. Crawford (Utah -6.5) : Could the Bearcats put it together in consecutive weeks against top-10 conference opponents? I'll lean no, but it'll be competitive. I was impressed with the Utes' performance last week against Houston, coming back from 10 points down to thwart the Cougars' road upset bid. Utah is now my projected favorite in the conference, and a win this weekend sets up fireworks against BYU on Nov. 7. Just don't get caught looking ahead in this trap spot. ... Utah 34, Cincinnati 24. No. 20 Northwestern at Oregon (-3.5) Hummer ( Northwestern +3.5) : It's a Chip Kelly reunion in Eugene! On paper, Oregon should have an advantage up front because the Wildcats are one of the worst pass-blocking units in the FBS. But … Oregon is 110th nationally in pressure created on passing downs. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 28, 2026 at 5:02 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's Ohio State. It's among the most super of superpowers. It's one of those programs with no excuses. It gets just about any player it wants, its realistic expectations are national title or bust, and it's one of the few programs that can lose its starting quarterback and still reasonably be considered the No. 1 team in the country. But now it has to go at least the next several weeks without star quarterback Julian Sayin, who injured his shoulder in the win over Indiana a few weeks ago. There's a quarterback battle to see who steps into the role as the team travels to Los Angeles to face a desperate USC team in a whole lot of trouble. The Trojans are 6-2, but they just got stuffed by Wisconsin in a punishing 24-7 loss, and with a brutal schedule to close, the Lincoln Riley hot seat is flaming. On the plus side, win, and the team is still deep in the College Football Playoff hunt. Ohio State vs USC: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for USC with a trip to Indiana next after a week off, and then Maryland, and it all closes at UCLA. Ohio State finishes with three of its last four games in Columbus, hosting Oregon next week. The road game is at Nebraska. This is the first time these two have met since a 24-7 Ohio State win in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. USC has won seven or the last eight in the series goning back to the 1974 Rose Bowl. How To Watch Ohio State vs USC Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, CA – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Ohio State Will Win USC just isn't that great. It has a wonderful 6-2 record, quarterback Jayden Maiava is terrific, and there's still pop and explosion to worry about, but there are flaws. It beat Washington and Penn State, but lost at home to a struggling Oregon, and couldn't get anything going against the Badgers. Ohio State isn't the Ohio State of previous seasons, but it's still good enough to beat anyone else this year. To win, the Buckeyes have to screw up, but USC doesn't take the ball away with just six turnovers forced on the season, and there's little running game to worry about. USC ran well on Rutgers and Louisiana, and that's about it. Slow down the midrange USC passing game, slow down USC. Why USC Will Win If Ohio State didn't exactly go turn-it-loose full-throttle with Julian Sayin under center, what will it do with Luke Fahey and/or Tavien St. Clair? Both are talented prospects, and no matter who is under center, there's still Jeremiah Smith and a loaded receiving corps to throw to, but this is where the offense has to rely on the running game, and it might not be able to do it. The Buckeyes are averaging a pedestrian four yards per carry, and were stuffed by Indiana two weeks ago, gaining just 37 yards. Fahey missed both of his throws against Indiana, and St. Clair has only seen the lightest of mop-up work so far. Ohio State vs USC Prediction, Betting Lines Which team has another gear? Can USC's run defense ball out, and can Jayden Maiava play like the best quarterback on the field? Or will the Ohio State defense step up and keep the big pass plays to a minimum? Yes, Indiana came within a few inches from beating Ohio State, but Josh Hoover only hit 50% of his passes, and only Arch Manning has been able to complete more than 56% against the Buckeyes. Maiava will have a nice day, but the Trojans will stall a bit too often. It won't be pretty, but the Buckeyes will take advantage of a few good field position chances to survive and advance in a relatively low-scoring game. Ohio State 23, USC 16 Latest Consensus Line: Ohio State -6.5, o/u: 51.5 ATS Confidence (out of 5) : 2.5 Must See Rating (out of 5) : 4 Consensus line based on BetMGM, Caesars, DraftKings, and FanDuel. picks.headline: Ohio State Gets Excellent Prediction Ahead of USC Showdown
picks.blurb: Ohio State Gets Excellent Prediction Ahead of USC Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Drew Rasmussen starting Game 5 NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Ohio State Gets Excellent Prediction Ahead of USC Showdown (Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch / USA TODA) Matt Levine Mon, October 26, 2026 at 7:07 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Ohio State Buckeyes are gearing up for a big game this weekend as the team heads to the West Coast. After a bye week, the Buckeyes will now be facing off against the USC Trojans, giving this team another test to overcome. Ohio State remains one of the better teams in the country, but the Trojans will be a challenge. This will be the first game between the two historic programs in Big Ten play, giving each another reason to want to win. The two programs have met multiple times over the years, and it's always been a fun matchup. The Buckeyes did lose starting quarterback Julian Sayin, likely for the season, but this team still has a lot of talent on the roster. Ohio State believes that it can still win a title this season, and the Trojans are just the next team in its way. As the team gets ready for the Trojans, they will be entering the game with a record of 6-1, going 4-0 in Big Ten play. USC comes in with a record of 6-2, going 3-2 in their conference games so far. The Trojans are coming off a bad loss to the Wisconsin Badgers last weekend, giving this team all the desperation they need. The Buckeyes will need to stay focused in this game, looking at this trip as purely business. Entering the game, the Buckeyes are still favored to take down the Trojans, even with the injury to Sayin. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Ohio State has an 82.8 percent chance of defeating USC on the road this week. For the Buckeyes, making sure to keep the basics the same in this game will be a key. Even without Sayin, the offense should still run through star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, giving the team a boost. Ohio State may rely even more heavily on Smith to help whoever is under center for this Buckeyes team, giving them a reliable target. Smith is on pace for a truly special season, and the loss of Sayin shouldn't change that fact. The Buckeyes defense will also be tasked with slowing down USC quarterback Jayden Maiava, who has thrown for 2,302 yards with 19 touchdowns and five interceptions. The Trojans rely on their offense to set the tone for the team, and the defense has been a little shaky this season. Kickoff between the two sides is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

We have a number of intriguing matchups this week, and it all starts on Friday night. To kick off my Week 9 betting card, I'm looking toward a Big 12 battle between the Baylor Bears — who just fired their head coach — and the UCF Knights, who just pulled off their first-ever upset over a top-five team. On Saturday, we'll begin in Iowa City, where the Iowa Hawkeyes will look to bounce back in a trophy game against the No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers. Then, in the SEC, the No. 17 Florida Gators meet the No. 3 Georgia Bulldogs for the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party in Atlanta. Finally, to close it all out, we'll take a look at a Big Ten tilt between the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes and USC Trojans. With so much to get to, let's dive into my college football picks and NCAAF predictions for the Week 9 games on Saturday, October 31. Baylor has fired head coach Dave Aranda, a move made after a critical loss to Kansas in Week 8. The former LSU defensive coordinator leaves Waco with a 40-40 overall mark, not good enough for the current administration. Former athletic director Mack Rhoades took a separation agreement in November 2025, leaving Aranda's future in doubt under new athletic director Doug McNamee. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman, recently brought in from Kansas State , will serve as the interim coach as Baylor looks to reach bowl season. The Baylor defense was never the issue this season, allowing an average of 16.1 points per game. The offense, under transfer quarterback DJ Lagway, has severely struggled with coordinator Jake Spavital. The Bears sit outside the top 110 in Success Rate on offense, relying on pass explosives as the only means of creating scoring opportunities. Despite the struggles as a whole, Lagway has seen improvement from his days at Florida with an increase in big-time throws and a lower turnover-worthy play rate. The Bears struggle in scoring position, averaging just 3.3 points on 50 offensive possessions inside the opponent's 40-yard line. Red-zone efficiency has been a constant failure all season, ranking 121st in touchdown percentage. Only half of the 30 possessions that made it into the red zone have resulted in a Baylor touchdown. UCF had one of the more advantageous spots of the entire college football calendar when hosting BYU , as the Cougars were coming off a program-defining win over Notre Dame . The overtime game provided all the thrills for a college football masterpiece, as the Knights took a field-storming victory with an 89% post-game win expectancy. Backup quarterback Keyone Jenkins led UCF to four methodical drives and an explosive passing attack, tossing six explosives through the air. The defense had the assignment of slowing down Heisman hopeful Bear Bachmeier , and it limited the BYU quarterback to just 37 rushing yards on 15 carries. The biggest factor was basic fundamentals, as the Knights missed just nine tackles in the game to add on a PFF tackling grade that ranks in the top 25. The Cougars' high-octane offense was limited to just a single rush explosive. It makes sense considering UCF's defense ranks 15th in Line Yards and top-40 in Rush EPA allowed. The handicap on this game forces handicappers to look beyond the advanced statistics, as the Baylor program is in flux. Klanderman isn't expected to win the job as Baylor's head coach, as McNamee has made it clear a coach with Texas roots and an offensive mindset will be the next hire. The downstream effect of the coaching search could create outside noise for coordinators and players looking for their next stop if they don't make a bowl game. Statistically, Baylor could have a hard time generating points against the UCF defense. The Bears have generated plenty of available yards to create scoring opportunities, but a rank outside the top 100 in Finishing Drives will go against a Knights defense that's 32nd in limiting opponents in scoring position. With the expectation that UCF will have a hangover from one of the most electric college football games of the season, a first-half under is the look from a statistical and spot perspective. There are also advantages for UCF in the run game against the Baylor defense. The Bears have a top-10 unit in terms of Rushing Success Rate allowed but have a mid-FBS average of 50% against teams that use inside zone. The Knights run a heavy amount of inside zone through Jenkins and running back Duke Watson . A boost could be in store if quarterback Alonza Barnett III returns from a hamstring injury. The James Madison transfer suited up for the BYU game but did not play for the fifth straight game. Any contribution from Barnett would further solidify UCF's position. Pick: 1H Under 24.5 · UCF ML (-110 or Better) Florida entered the bye week on a high note, beating a top-10 team on the road for the first time since 2012. The Gators remain at two losses on the season in the thick of the SEC race and a potential spot in the College Football Playoff, but a date with Georgia in the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party comes first. The biggest takeaway from the victory over Texas came from backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. tossing a couple of touchdowns in a mistake-free game. The sophomore completed 22-of-35 passes while chipping in 50 rushing yards with an even split of scrambles and designed run calls. On the other side, the defense continues to rank as one of the best in the nation when creating chaos. The top-10 Havoc numbers are led by 53 tackles for loss , nine forced fumbles and 34 passes defensed. Five players on the defensive line have generated double-digit pressures, while seven different defenders have multiple pass breakups. The issue with Florida's defense is its performance close to the goal line, ranking 95th in red-zone defense. The Gators have allowed 40 opponent possessions to cross the 40-yard line and are giving up an average of 4.4 points per trip . Georgia's first loss to Auburn in nine years comes as a result of ball protection. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was responsible for two interceptions and a fumble, an uncharacteristic set of events for the senior. Up until the Alabama game in Week 6, Stockton managed to throw just six interceptions and lose three fumbles since the beginning of the 2025 season. In the past two games, the Georgia quarterback has committed two fumbles and three interceptions . There's the case that Stockton had too much of the load against Auburn, taking a critical hit in the first series of the game. Running back Chauncey Bowens has missed multiple games with injury, while Nate Frazier was ineffective coming off a rib injury, finishing with less than 20 rushing yards. away.headline: What is the status of Ohio State's Kenyatta Jackson Jr., Jay Timmons?
away.blurb: "Last week was a great opportunity to get a bunch of guys some rest," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said. "We'll see how this week goes. ... [Most] will probably go through the rest of the week, and as we get closer to the game, we'll get an idea." Jackson was helped to the medical tent by two Ohio State athletic trainers with 11:55 remaining in the Buckeyes ' 19-15 road win on Oct. 17. He returned for the Hoosiers' final drive but then had to be helped by defensive tackle Eddrick Houston and a trainer going back to the locker room. The fifth-year defender provides crucial experience, as he's the only remaining Ohio State defensive lineman who appeared in all 16 games during the 2024 national championship run. Along with leading the Buckeyes in sacks this season (3), Jackson has played 320 snaps, according to PFF – 63 more than any other Ohio State defensive lineman. Of Jackson's 22 tackles, seven came against the Hoosiers, marking his career high. Timmons also had a career game in Bloomington, recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble, before being sidelined for Ohio State's final defensive drives. The freshman was dealing with an unspecified injury leading up to the Indiana game, missing the previous two matchups. In his first four Ohio State games, Timmons logged nine tackles, four pass breakups and a forced fumble in the opening drive against Texas. He was initially hurt in the third quarter against Illinois on Sept. 26. No. 2 Ohio State will travel to face No. 15 Southern California on Oct. 31.

After USC's performance in Madison, however, that possibility went out the window, and "GameDay" will instead head to Minnesota- Indiana . Someday, "College GameDay" will finally return to USC. This week, however, the Trojans will be back home at the Coliseum to take on Ohio State. The matchup between the Gophers and the Hoosiers is a rather interesting choice, given that Minnesota is unranked, Indiana is favored by nearly three touchdowns, and ESPN is not even televising the game. This strongly suggests that the show had another game in mind, but had to pivot at the last minute due to an upset. In other words, USC had an absolutely golden opportunity to finally bring "GameDay" back to the Coliseum for the first time in 13 years—an astonishing streak for one of the premier programs in the sport. However, Lincoln Riley blew it, and instead, the drought will continue. From 2004 through 2013, the Trojans hosted "GameDay" at least once in all but two years—including twice in 2006. However, due to a combination of down years for the program and ESPN placing an increased emphasis on the SEC, "GameDay" has not returned to the Coliseum since USC upset Stanford in 2013. Austin Kawecki is trending in the right direction Starting center Austin Kawecki left in the middle of the Badgers’ game with Michigan State in Week 5. On top of that, the cornerback depth has already taken a hit this year after Cai Bates was lost for the season with a knee injury early in the year. Losing Coleman wouldn’t be ideal, either. But the passing attack for the Badgers has been inconsistent, and even after his breakout game against Notre Dame in Week 1, he hasn’t been the force we all hoped he’d be. Fortunately for the Badgers, they just got Jaylon Domingeaux back from injury last week and caught a pair of passes, so there is at least some more depth at receiver. home.headline: JuJu Watkins Gives Confident Quote in Return from Major Injury for USC
home.blurb: "Coming back, I haven't lost my confidence, I haven't lost my attention to detail," the senior guard said, per Beth Harris of the Associated Press. "Everything is the same, it's just I've been out for a minute." Now, Watkins can play off Jazzy Davidson, who led the Trojans in the five main stat categories a season ago. Five-star recruit Saniyah Hall could make a big impact right out of the gate as well. She scored a team-high 23 points Sunday. USC star JuJu Watkins doesn't think her game has suffered much after she missed an entire season due to a torn ACL. Watkins shook off some of the rust in Sunday's 78-76 exhibition victory over California. She played 22 minutes, finishing with 18 points on 6-of-14 shooting. Former UConn star Paige Bueckers was a two-time All-American in her final two years after tearing her ACL in 2022, and she was instrumental in the Huskies' 2025 national championship. Watkins could easily be just as sharp as she was before her injury. One nice thing for the 2025 national player of the year, given any lingering effects from the ACL tear, is that she shouldn't have to shoulder the kind of offensive burden she did in her first two years. As a true freshman, the 6'2" playmaker led Division I in usage rate (42.7 percent), per Sports Reference . That number dropped a bit but remained high (32.8 percent) in 2024-25. Watkins believes "there's no ceiling" to what USC can achieve and she might be right. The Trojans are third behind South Carolina and UConn in the preseason AP Top 25 . The team's talent extends well beyond Watkins, but she'll undoubtedly play a big role on whether a deep tournament run is in store this coming spring.

home.headline: “College GameDay” passes up on USC-Ohio State after Trojans’ loss
home.blurb: In recent weeks, there had been speculation that ESPN's "College GameDay" could finally return to Los Angeles for the matchup of college football blue bloods. After USC's performance in Madison, however, that possibility went out the window, and "GameDay" will instead head to Minnesota- Indiana . Someday, "College GameDay" will finally return to USC. Right now, however, it appears as though that return will be under a different head coach. “College GameDay” passes up on USC-Ohio State after Trojans’ loss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF “College GameDay” passes up on USC-Ohio State after Trojans’ loss Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads On Saturday evening, the USC football team suffered an embarrassing 24-7 road loss to Wisconsin . This week, however, the Trojans will be back home at the Coliseum to take on Ohio State. The matchup between the Gophers and the Hoosiers is a rather interesting choice, given that Minnesota is unranked, Indiana is favored by nearly three touchdowns, and ESPN is not even televising the game. This strongly suggests that the show had another game in mind, but had to pivot at the last minute due to an upset. In other words, USC had an absolutely golden opportunity to finally bring "GameDay" back to the Coliseum for the first time in 13 years—an astonishing streak for one of the premier programs in the sport. However, Lincoln Riley blew it, and instead, the drought will continue. From 2004 through 2013, the Trojans hosted "GameDay" at least once in all but two years—including twice in 2006. However, due to a combination of down years for the program and ESPN placing an increased emphasis on the SEC, "GameDay" has not returned to the Coliseum since USC upset Stanford in 2013. picks.blurb: Prediction for Baylor's game at UCF: Can Bears give interim coach a winning start? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Drew Rasmussen starting Game 5 NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips LAWRENCE, KANSAS - OCTOBER 24: Gavin Freeman #6 of the Baylor Bears hauls in a catch during the first quarter of the game against the Kansas Jayhawks on October 24, 2026 at the David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium in Lawrence, Kansas. (Photo by Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) (Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Imag) Rylie Painter Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Baylor at UCF 6:30 p.m. Friday at Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando, Fla. Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12); UCF (4-3, 2-2). Last meeting: Baylor beat UCF 30-3 on Nov. 1, 2025, in Waco What's at stake? This is an important opportunity for Baylor to get its season back on track. The Bears have dropped consecutive games against TCU and Kansas and now enter a new chapter under interim head coach Joe Klanderman following Dave Aranda's dismissal . At 4-3, Baylor cannot afford to let another conference game slip away if it hopes to remain competitive in the Big 12 standings. A road win would also give Klanderman a strong start to his tenure. UCF enters the matchup with momentum after defeating No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime. The Knights have shown they can compete with the conference's top teams, making Friday's matchup an important test for Baylor's defense. When Baylor has the ball Baylor's passing attack will be one of its biggest advantages in this matchup. The Bears average 278.9 passing yards per game, and UCF surrenders 239.7 passing yards per game. Quarterback DJ Lagway will need to take advantage of that matchup and find opportunities downfield. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has been one of Baylor's most consistent weapons, recording 58 receptions for 678 yards through seven games. His ability to create plays and stretch the field could be important against a UCF defense that has struggled more against the pass than the run. However, Baylor will need to establish a more consistent rushing attack. Dawson Pendergrass leads the Bears with 331 rushing yards, but the offense has averaged just 146.1 rushing yards per game. Finding balance between the run and pass will be important in keeping UCF's defense from focusing entirely on Lagway. When UCF has the ball The Knights rely on a balanced offensive attack led by quarterback Keyone Jenkins and running back Duke Watson. Jenkins has thrown for 1,099 yards and 11 touchdowns while Watson leads the team with 577 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Baylor's defensive front will need to pressure Jenkins and limit Watson's ability to establish the run. The Bears rank third nationally in sacks, giving them an opportunity to disrupt UCF's offensive rhythm. If Baylor can force third-and-long situations and create turnovers, it could make things difficult for a UCF offense that is coming off an emotional double-overtime victory. Baylor enters this matchup with plenty to prove after consecutive losses and a coaching change. While UCF has momentum following its win over BYU, the Bears have the defensive talent to make this a difficult matchup for the Knights. I expect Baylor to lean on its defense and take advantage of its passing game, with Freeman playing an important role. The Bears will need to clean up their mistakes and avoid giving UCF extra opportunities, but the Bears will find a way to get their first win under Klanderman. Score: Baylor 27, UCF 24. UCF enters the game riding high after stunning No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime for the Knights' biggest win since joining the Big 12. Meanwhile, Baylor is beginning a new era after firing head coach Dave Aranda following Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas, with defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman taking over as interim head coach. Despite taking very different paths to get here, Baylor and UCF enter Friday night's game with identical 4-3 overall records and 2-2 marks in Big 12 play. For UCF, the question is whether Scott Frost's team can build off its breakthrough win or suffer a letdown. For Baylor, it's about what kind of response the Bears will have in their first game without Aranda. Here is everything you need to know about Baylor vs. UCF in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Friday night's Big 12 matchup. Baylor vs. UCF Odds Spread: UCF -1.5 Over/Under: 48.5 Moneyline: UCF -120/Baylor +100 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: How do the emotions play a factor? The emotions on both sides of this game are tremendous. UCF is coming off of one of the biggest wins in program history over No. 2 BYU in double overtime at home. Now, they have to put that in the rearview mirror and take on Baylor. What' done is done. Have the Knights spent the last week in celebration mode? And then, on the other side, head coach Dave Aranda was fired on Sunday by Baylor. How does the team respond? How does defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman do in the interim role? There are so many unknowns going into this game, beyond the X's and O's, that ultimately will determine the outcome. Baylor vs. UCF Prediction and Pick Prediction: UCF 23, Baylor 20 It's a short week for both teams, but the good news for UCF is that they're playing their second-straight home game after a bye week. They haven't had to leave the friendly confines of Central Florida in nearly a month. Meantime, Baylor is getting set for its 3rd road game in its last four match ups, and their first without Aranda. In games like this, I try to find a nugget to sway me one way or the other, and here's what I've found: Baylor leads the Big 12 with 27 sacks in seven games. But one of the many things that UCF has done well with Keyone Jenkins is move the pocket, get rid of the ball quickly and avoid pressure in the backfield. BYU only had one sack last week against UCF, and the Knights have only allowed 10 in seven games, good for fourth fewest in the Big 12 Conference. Negating the pass rush by Baylor opens up a lot of opportunities for the UCF offense, and I believe that will be a game-changer on Friday night. Baylor has proven it can play with, and beat, some of the lesser Big 12 teams like Colorado and Arizona State. But even against just slightly better competition, TCU and Kansas, they came up short. UCF is one of the more underrated teams in the country, which I've been telling you since August. And despite their injuries, they're playing solid, team football, and that culminated with a with vs. BYU. But it was not a fluke. They led Houston in the second half on the road. They were beating Oklahoma State in Stillwater early in the game. This team can play with the best. Now, they get a chance to play one of the worst? I'll not overcomplicate this and take UCF to win and cover. Baylor's run defense ranks 4th in the Big 12, but they've already played the three worst running teams in the conference in Colorado, Arizona State and TCU. Now, they get Duke Watson, Jenkins and the rest of the run game going on Friday night to seal a win. UCF wins. UCF covers. Baylor vs. UCF Three games are on the college football card for Friday night, headlined by Baylor vs. UCF. Both teams are in very difficult spots here, as the Knights just upset BYU at home in overtime last week and the Bears fired head coach Dave Aranda after losing at home to Kansas. On a night with the MAC, American, and Big 12, we have Kent State as a rare home favorite, a mediocre Tulane team laying double digits, and then the coin flip in Orlando. Despite the tricky circumstances with Baylor and UCF, that’s the game of the night and the game that deserves the most attention. Odds from Circa Sports as of October 28, 1:20 p.m. PT ; check out our Circa Betting Splits and DraftKings Betting Splits . See all of our Week 9 College Football Picks and Predictions . Baylor at UCF (-1, 48) Prediction Friday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN) Baylor invades the Bounce House this week and we’ll see if interim head coach Joe Klanderman can put some more pep in the steps of the Bears. It felt like Aranda was simply holding on for dear life with this gig for a while and it finally came to a head this past week with a blocked field goal that led to a loss against the Jayhawks. I watched Klanderman’s media availability this week and he comes across as a very honest, very poignant guy who isn’t going to BS this team about what’s going on. I appreciate that. In this day and age, I think the players do as well. Klanderman will continue to call the defense, while longtime up-and-comer Jake Spavital has creative freedom on offense. The 41-year-old Spavital was Texas A&M’s OC by the age of 30 and even was Texas State’s head coach for four rough seasons. But he’s always been pretty highly-regarded in the coaching world and now he has free reign of the offense. By no means has the offense been good, but Aranda was kind of a passive guy and there wasn’t a lot of explosiveness or aggressiveness to Baylor’s offensive profile. With a lot of money invested in DJ Lagway, let’s see if Spavital can unlock something. Lagway has only completed 52.1% of his passes and only has 26 carries for 19 yards, so it’s been a struggle to get him free. Leading rusher Dawson Pendergrass only has 3.5 yards per carry. The Baylor offensive line needs to be better, but we should see an improvement in effort and focus for this week. UCF head coach Scott Frost brought in Keyone Jenkins as an insurance policy behind expected starter Alonza Barrett III from James Madison. Instead, it has been Jenkins, the FIU transfer, who has carried this team in Barrett’s absence. He sports an 11/3 TD/INT ratio and a completion rate butting up against 70%, while transfer RB Duke Watson has rushed for 6.8 yards per carry. While Baylor’s defensive numbers stand up a lot better, as the Bears are 17th in the nation in yards per play allowed, it should be noted that Jeff Sagarin has a strength of schedule gap of 30 spots between the two teams, as UCF has already played three top-30 teams per Sagarin and Baylor has not played any. The Knights rank 27th in SOS and the Bears are 57th, with a big difference in Big 12 opponents. UCF has played TCU, Houston, Oklahoma State, and BYU. Baylor has played Colorado, Arizona State, TCU, and Kansas. Of that group, Arizona State is the only one with a winning record and the only one without a losing conference record. It’s a tough spot for UCF coming off of the BYU win, but they aren’t traveling, they don’t have the internal tumult, and Jenkins has definitively outplayed Lagway this season and even done so against better competition. Other Friday Games Tulane (-10, 47) at Charlotte: This is a hefty number for Tulane, a team that ranks 99th with -.51 net points per drive per Brian Fremeau of BCFToys. Of course, Charlotte is 134th out of 138 teams, so we’re talking about one of the worst programs in the nation. The Green Wave have not gotten good QB play out of either Kadin Semonza or Trace Johnson, with 18 total sacks and a 5/5 TD/INT ratio. Even though the Green Wave have a great running game and maybe that will be enough, winning by margin requires taking care of the football and avoiding negative plays. Charlotte has poor run defense numbers, but it should be noted that they’ve allowed 4.55 YPC to FBS opponents and allowed 5.36 YPC in the loss to The Citadel. Kent State (-10, 46.5) at Sacramento State: Historical outliers are scary and Kent State being favored like this on the road hasn’t happened since 2022. That could be part of the reason why we’ve seen money come in on the Hornets and against the Golden Flashes. It’s also just ludicrous to think about Kent State facing these kinds of expectations, but Sac State might be the worst FBS team we’ve ever seen. If Kent wins and covers, that might solidify it, but that’s an enormous ask and the market seems to think it’s too big of one. away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship. Aranda eventually became much more aggressive in the portal, but the adjustment came after Baylor had already fallen behind. 2. Failing to Balance NIL Investments Acros

Should he be able to play, he could serve as an emergency backup to Jenkins should he get injured during the game. The Knights' secondary took another hit this week as starting safety Demari Henderson has been ruled out for Friday's Space Game. It will be the first time Henderson has missed a game since he missed a majority of the 2024 season. He joins cornerback DJ Bell , who was ruled out for a second straight week. Maiava was designated as probable and was a game-time decision against BYU, so he is trending towards returning on Friday. Fellow offensive lineman Preston Cushman was also designated probable. Meanwhile, Spell's name is nowhere to be found in Tuesday's report, which could mean one of two things: he is available to play on Friday, or he has been designated out for the season. Frost said back on Sep. 19 that Spell had "a bit of plantar fasciitis," a condition that has different recovery times depending on the severity. So, whether Spell suits up on Friday against Baylor will be telling on his availability going forward. However, there was one offensive lineman ruled out for Friday: Tyler Gibson . It is set to be his third consecutive missed game. After making his 2026 debut on Saturday against BYU, Duane Thomas Jr. is now designated as probable for Friday's matchup against Baylor. home.blurb: The Knights listed 10 players, including starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III and freshman running back Taevion Swing (162 yards), as questionable or worse on Thursday. Another six players – 4 defense, 1 offense, 1 special teams – are probable for the week's top-10 home test vs. No. 2 BYU, which is hot off its nationally-regarded win over then-No. 2 Notre Dame in Provo. It'll be up to Jenkins, who left the game for UCF in the third quarter of the Houston loss , to test BYU through the air on Saturday with Barnett unavailable, and it'll come as the senior backup grows comfortable as his team's signal caller. The Scott Frost staff displays trust in Jenkins, but the payout hasn't come in the win column following two Big 12 losses at Oklahoma State and Houston; Both losses saw Jenkins combine for 518 passing yards, 5 touchdowns and two interceptions on 53 attempts. To stay within such a low spread, UCF needs a big day out of Jenkins and the offense to keep pace with a BYU squad intent on keeping its perfect 3-0 Big 12 record intact. It's hard to bet against the Cougars, but this home return for UCF after a week off certainly factors into the math as Frost and company look for a big one this weekend when the league's frontrunners come to town. On Wednesday, UCF released the most-recent injury report, with 16 Knights dealing with ailments. This is extremely-promising signs for UCF's offensive outlook, as he would add a big element to the Knights' passing game ahead of their showdown with No. 2 BYU . Despite initial reports confirming Barnett will not make the start on Saturday, fffensive coordinator Steve Cooper spoke to the media on Tuesday, saying that he thinks there is a fair chance Barnett could see action. Head coach Scott Frost gave promising remarks as well, adding that Barnett is making "really good progress" in his recovery. With the Cougars' offense clicking at a high level, getting Barnett back would help the Knights keep up with the top squad in the conference. On defense, UCF will still be without star linebacker Lewis Carter , who has continued to miss time after a strong early start to his senior campaign. Carter showed the ability to produce against some of the top competition in the conference last season, posting big showings towards the end of the year. In three of the final four games of the season, Carter recorded 12 or more tackles, doing so against Texas Tech , Houston, and the looming BYU Cougars. BYU's run game is one of the offense's biggest strengths, which will be difficult to slow down without Carter in the middle. Last season against BYU, UCF got off to a hot start, and it began to look like the Knights could upset the Cougars and potentially earn a bowl bid. This time around, Frost is hoping to get off to a hot start and maintain it throughout the game - something that the Knights have not been able to do against Oklahoma State and Houston in the past weeks.
